areas_reviewed.label: Automated Driving Planning
areas_reviewed.boundary: Select behaviors and generate feasible, rule-aware paths and trajectories from mission goals, maps, perceived objects, vehicle state and operating constraints; prediction estimates other agents, while planning selects ego behavior and motion.
areas_reviewed.key_boundary: Prediction trajectories are inputs/conditioning for behavior or motion planning, not themselves an ego plan. A planner trajectory is an input to a controller; that interface does not make planning a tracking-control task. nuPlan and nuPlan-R are simulation/benchmark evidence, not on-road safety or regulatory approval.

areas_reviewed.label: Vehicle Control and Dynamics
areas_reviewed.boundary: Translate a target trajectory or motion request into stable steering, braking and acceleration commands using vehicle state, dynamics, actuator limits and feedback; distinguish this from generating the target path/trajectory.
areas_reviewed.key_boundary: Autoware documentation distinguishes trajectory tracking/control commands from vehicle-specific drive-by-wire adaptation. Conventional geometric/PID and optimization/MPC methods are alternatives or complements depending on the control problem; a controller output is consumed by the vehicle interface, but neither architecture adjacency nor one benchmark establishes a universal dependency.

areas_reviewed.label: Vehicle Interface and System Integration
areas_reviewed.boundary: Integrate ADS software, compute, sensors, networks and vehicle subsystems; translate normalized commands/status into platform-specific protocols and actuations, and diagnose end-to-end timing, state and mode behavior.
areas_reviewed.key_boundary: A vehicle adapter converts generalized control requests to platform-specific torque, pressure, pedal or equivalent commands and returns status. Application algorithms (planner/controller) and vehicle integration are distinct. AUTOSAR, ROS conventions and interface examples are implementation/context evidence, not universal requirements or safety certification.

areas_reviewed.label: ADS Safety, Verification and Validation
areas_reviewed.boundary: Define safety requirements/ODD and build evidence across component, vehicle and ADS lifecycle tests; keep E/E malfunction functional safety, intended-function insufficiency (SOTIF), ADS-level safety argument, simulation, closed-course/on-road testing and type approval distinct.
areas_reviewed.key_boundary: ISO 26262 addresses E/E functional-safety malfunction hazards; ISO 21448 addresses hazards from functional insufficiency/performance limits and reasonably foreseeable misuse; UL 4600 is an autonomy safety-case framework. A simulation result is one evidence layer, not proof of physical validity, road safety, legal permission or type approval.

cell_disposition_register.claim: Classical AV design decomposes route planning, behavior decision, motion planning and vehicle control; planners must account for environment structure, vehicle model and computational constraints.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Paden et al. (2016), Sections II-IV; see source-index entry D166-PADEN-PLANNING-CONTROL-SURVEY-2016.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Planning outputs a selected ego behavior/path/trajectory, not other-agent predictions or actuator commands.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: planning architecture taxonomy
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Mission goal, road/map representation, perceived scene, ego state, selected vehicle model and computational/operational constraints.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Route, behavior decision and motion path/trajectory as distinct planning artifacts; actuator commands belong to downstream feedback control.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: Paden et al.'s urban-vehicle survey uses a modular conceptual decomposition and explicitly allows architecture partitions to vary; it does not assert one universal production stack.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: Survey reflects its 2016 review scope and is not a present-day complete taxonomy or mandated order.

relationship_evidence.explanation: Vehicle/road geometry and state are inputs to the planning design; the paper describes model assumptions, not a universal training sequence.

cell_disposition_register.review_note: The mapped disposition is terminal for this cell candidate; required mapping fields are present. Area-level source saturation is assessed separately.

cell_disposition_register.claim: Current ADS planning foundations include treating the operational design domain as explicit where/when capability limits and recognizing that interactive maneuvers such as merges and unprotected turns may require joint multi-agent motion forecasts rather than isolated per-object prediction; the applicable ODD and evidence remain system- and jurisdiction-specific.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Waymo Open Motion Dataset author/publisher page, abstract: interactive merges/unprotected turns and the statement that joint predictions of multiple objects are required for effective route planning; NHTSA ADS 2.0 (2017), Section 1 'Operational Design Domain', PDF pp. 11-12, defining where/when capability limits and encouraging documented assessment/testing/validation for the prescribed ODD.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Current planning foundation for interactive-agent reasoning and ODD-bounded behavior; NHTSA is U.S. voluntary guidance and the Waymo source is a research-data/forecasting contribution, not a universal legal or algorithm mandate.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: ODD and interactive-prediction planning competency
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Roadway/geographic/speed/environmental operating limits, map and ego state, and relevant other-agent histories or forecasts in interactive maneuvers.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: An ego behavior/path/trajectory decision conditioned on the declared operating limits and interaction-relevant agent hypotheses, with validation scope tied to the prescribed ODD.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: Waymo's paper establishes a research-data and forecasting need for joint predictions in interactive examples, while NHTSA describes an ODD framework and voluntary U.S. practices; neither requires one specific planner architecture.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: Waymo's page is an author/publisher summary of a 2021 dataset paper, not proof that joint prediction improves every planner. NHTSA ADS 2.0 is voluntary and U.S.-scoped, not Nigerian law. Neither source defines a complete local road-rule model or demonstrates any system's safety.

relationship_evidence.explanation: A planner's intended behavior and evaluation conditions depend on its system ODD; in interactive maneuvers, other-agent motion hypotheses can condition ego behavior selection, but this does not prescribe a universal prediction module or sequence.

remaining_scope: Vehicle/road geometry and uncertainty propagation, jurisdiction-specific traffic-rule representation (including Nigeria), planning behavior/path/trajectory alternatives, and operating-domain monitoring/fallback remain open.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: Mapped a bounded foundation claim; FRSC training guidance adds local road-condition context but does not resolve gazetted rule representation, ADS authorization, ODD-specific curricula or full planning-method coverage.

cell_disposition_register.claim: Emerging research increasingly couples multi-agent behavior prediction with ego planning; the NeurIPS 2024 BeTop study proposes topological joint-behavior representations and contingency learning to guide interactive trajectory generation, but reports benchmark evidence rather than deployed-road validation.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Liu et al., NeurIPS 2024, Sections 1 and 3-4; abstract and pp. 1-2 on scene uncertainty, dense/sparse representations and prediction-planning integration; methods/results on topology-guided joint behaviors and contingency planning.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Emerging algorithmic planning competency at the prediction/decision boundary: jointly reason over interacting agents to produce a compliant ego trajectory; other-agent trajectories remain inputs/latent hypotheses rather than the ego plan.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: research method and planning competency
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Scene-agent histories, multi-agent future behavior hypotheses, ego context and interactive scenario representations.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Predicted joint behavioral topology and a contingency-aware ego trajectory, evaluated on the paper's nuPlan/WOMD datasets and interactive benchmark.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The paper's datasets, training labels, architecture and benchmark define its reported setting; its claimed state-of-the-art results are author-reported research results, not independently replicated deployment findings.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: NeurIPS 2024 research paper and code/model release; results are dataset- and metric-specific, do not establish public-road use, safety validation, universal superiority or a required production architecture. Dense and sparse alternatives and uncertainty/compute trade-offs remain relevant.

relationship_evidence.explanation: Joint behavior reasoning conditions ego planning on interactive-agent hypotheses; the paper proposes integrated prediction/planning, but does not establish that every stack must couple modules or that this is a learning prerequisite.

remaining_scope: Learning-based planning, foundation/world models, end-to-end policies, interactive planning and autonomous racing methods; document the evidence and transfer boundary from competition/racing ODDs to public-road operation.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: Mapped one emerging research approach; cell's broader foundation/world-model, end-to-end, uncertainty and transfer scope remains open for counter-search.

cell_disposition_register.claim: A future-facing planning research capability is to evaluate candidate ego trajectories against action-conditioned future scene evolution and feed those predicted outcomes back into planning, rather than relying only on current observations or post-hoc scoring. ProDrive's 2026 CVPR workshop prototype demonstrates one query-centric planner/BEV-world-model coupling on NAVSIM v1; this is a research direction, not evidence of future industry adoption or validated road competence.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Fu et al., ProDrive, full arXiv manuscript Sections 1-3, PDF pp. 1-5 (planner/world-model architecture and coupling); Sections 4-5, pp. 6-8 (NAVSIM v1 test, metrics, ablations, future work).
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: A future-facing research capability documented by a present-day workshop prototype; the future horizon describes potential direction, not a prediction of deployment or curricular priority.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: candidate-conditioned future-scene reasoning for trajectory planning
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Multi-view camera images, LiDAR, ego state, candidate trajectories and planner-refined ego tokens; predicted BEV scene rollouts and learned reward signals condition candidate evaluation.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Multiple candidate ego trajectories, predicted future BEV scene states, candidate reward scores and a selected trajectory; future-aware gradients train the planner/world-model coupling.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The model's predicted future BEV features and reward labels remain sufficiently informative for the represented NAVSIM distribution; the paper's benchmark and training setup do not establish robustness outside that distribution.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: Single 2026 workshop prototype evaluated on the log-derived, non-reactive NAVSIM benchmark (136 test scenarios); no public-road/closed-loop vehicle validation, independent replication, broad ODD coverage, calibrated uncertainty or adoption evidence. The authors list more expressive world models as future work.

relationship_evidence.explanation: ProDrive couples prediction and planning internally, contrasting with reactive or modular pipelines and external post-hoc trajectory reranking; it is one research alternative, not a proven replacement.

remaining_scope: Compare world-model and reactive/modular/end-to-end alternatives, benchmark and ODD limits, uncertainty and safety constraints, code reproducibility, independent replication and physical vehicle transfer; distinguish demonstrated capability from future adoption.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: One future-facing research capability is mapped; the cell disposition and frontier task are terminal. Alternative methods, replication and transfer remain area-level saturation limits.

cell_disposition_register.claim: Foundational urban-vehicle planning literature distinguishes graph/search, sampling-based and trajectory-optimization approaches; their suitability depends on map/environment structure, vehicle-state constraints and the planning horizon, not a universal ranking or mandatory serial stack.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Paden et al. (2016), Sections II-IV, full 27-page PDF; Section IV method-family survey.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Established/traditional planning design alternatives reviewed for urban self-driving vehicles; choice depends on environment representation, vehicle constraints and planning scope.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: historical planning-method design taxonomy
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Mission or maneuver objective, map or sensed free-space representation, vehicle state/model and kinematic/dynamic feasibility constraints.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: A route, feasible geometric path or time-parameterized trajectory candidate, depending on the planning level and method.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: Paden et al.'s 2016 survey is treated as a review of established urban-vehicle method families, not a current prevalence census; graph-search, sampling/tree and variational optimization solve related but not identical formulations.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: The survey taxonomy does not establish which methods dominate current production, compare all implementations under common metrics, prove a universally superior method or establish road safety. Detailed interaction, road-rule and Nigerian ODD treatment remains part of open task work.

relationship_evidence.explanation: Graph/search, sampling and optimization are alternative or combined design families for route/path/trajectory problems under distinct representations and constraints; the source does not make them interchangeable in every scenario or a required learning sequence.

cell_disposition_register.review_note: Mapped historical method-family claim; comparative performance, interaction handling and rule/ODD constraints remain outside this cell claim and under task review.

cell_disposition_register.outputs: Open-loop prediction/planner metrics or closed-loop simulated behavior and score/rank under the benchmark's scenario and traffic assumptions.

cell_disposition_register.limitations: Finite benchmark scenarios, simulators and a preprint; neither establishes on-road validity nor universal ranking changes.

cell_disposition_register.claim: A current research taxonomy contrasts modular pipeline planning, with explicit route/behavior/trajectory interfaces, against end-to-end learned mappings from perception inputs toward trajectory or control outputs; the tradeoff includes traceability and fault localization versus learned integration/generalization challenges.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Teng et al. (2023), arXiv:2303.09824, Introduction I-A to I-D (HTML lines 17-38) and challenges/future perspectives (lines 61-96).
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: This is a method/design taxonomy at the planning system boundary; end-to-end scope can include perception and control, so outputs differ from a modular ego planner.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: method/design taxonomy
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Modular design uses upstream perception, localization, map/route, vehicle state and constraints; end-to-end designs may take raw or encoded sensor inputs.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Modular route/behavior/trajectory artifacts; end-to-end trajectory points or control commands depending on the design.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The survey's pipeline/end-to-end distinction is used as an architecture-level comparison, not as a statement that all end-to-end systems span the whole stack.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: Survey manuscript and incomplete algorithm-section extraction; it reports a research taxonomy, not universal industry prevalence, deployed performance or superiority. No detailed comparison of constituent planner algorithms is inferred.

relationship_evidence.explanation: The two designs can address driving decision/trajectory generation under different modularity and observability assumptions; end-to-end papers may output controls rather than a planner trajectory, so compare only when task/output contracts match.

cell_disposition_register.review_note: Mapped claim includes required item/input/output/assumption fields.

cell_disposition_register.claim: A current research frontier is interactive prediction-and-planning: rather than treating other-agent prediction as a one-way input to ego planning, the method jointly models how surrounding agents may react to the ego vehicle's candidate behavior and selects an ego trajectory using scene context, agent histories and predicted interactions. A 2026 peer-reviewed review distinguishes marginal prediction, conditional multi-agent prediction and interactive AV-agent planning, and surveys time-axis, agent-axis and hybrid interaction formulations; this is a research taxonomy, not evidence that interactive planning is universally deployed or safer.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Li, Zhang & Zhao (2026), Sections 1-2, lines 71-116 (sequential modular/end-to-end versus bidirectional interaction; task definitions); Section 4.3 (interactive prediction/planning paradigms and named examples); Sections 5-6 (open/closed-loop evaluation and safety, robustness, generalization and deployment limitations).
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Future/futuristic research frontier as documented in a 2026 review; the method is actively researched, not a distant speculative technology or demonstrated universal production architecture.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: interactive prediction-and-planning method family / joint modeling design
cell_disposition_register.inputs: HD map and traffic-scene context, AV and surrounding-agent histories, candidate ego behavior/trajectory, and conditional or interactive predictions of other agents' responses.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Joint or conditional surrounding-agent future trajectories and a selected ego-vehicle trajectory; exact representations and decoder outputs vary by formulation.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The review's formulations distinguish marginal prediction p(Y_i|X,I), conditional multi-agent prediction p(Y_SA|X,I), and ego-agent interactive planning Y_AV=L(Y_SA,X,I); utility depends on scene representation, prediction/planning coupling, training/evaluation setup and the required planner interface.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: This is a peer-reviewed literature review, not a new controlled comparison or deployment survey. The authors identify safety, robustness, generalization and simulation-to-real transfer as open problems. Interactive methods are not interchangeable with sequential modular stacks unless input/output contracts, latency, explainability and validation requirements are compatible. No universal performance or safety advantage is asserted.

relationship_evidence.explanation: The review contrasts sequential one-way modular prediction-to-planning pipelines with bidirectional interactive prediction/planning. These are alternative architectural formulations only when both solve the same ego-motion decision task and their output, timing and validation contracts are aligned; interaction is not an additional mandatory stage for every planner.

cell_disposition_register.review_note: This mapping fills the future-horizon methods cell for interactive prediction/planning only. It does not close the broader planning frontier/task: world-model and end-to-end methods, named algorithm comparisons, tools/data, deployment maturity and competition-to-road transfer remain under review.

cell_disposition_register.claim: Established motion-planning technique families include graph search, sampling/tree exploration and variational optimization; a trajectory candidate must be judged against the selected vehicle model, feasibility limits and task objective rather than by planner-family label alone.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Paden et al. (2016), Sections IV-A to IV-C and vehicle/control model assumptions in Sections II-III; CommonRoad Tutorial 2 scenario constraints at page lines 14-21.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Algorithms search/optimize an ego route/path/trajectory through an environment and vehicle model; they do not predict other-agent intent by definition.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: algorithm families
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Road/obstacle representation, start/goal or behavior target, ego state and a vehicle/dynamics feasibility model.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Candidate or selected path/trajectory, with feasibility/cost checks defined by implementation.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The method assumes a defined planning problem and environment model; interaction forecasts and safety validation may be separate components.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: Paden is a 2016 urban-vehicle survey and the CommonRoad tutorial is one benchmark case; examples do not rank families or establish performance across ODDs.

relationship_evidence.explanation: Search, sampling and optimization are alternative planning mechanisms when tasked with the same feasible path/trajectory output; they differ in representation, constraints, search budget and solution guarantees.

cell_disposition_register.review_note: Mapped claim includes required item/input/output/assumption fields.

cell_disposition_register.claim: A bounded CommonRoad 2023 competition report compares two materially different current motion-planning designs under shared interactive scenarios and compute limits: reachability-based decision-making plus optimization, and trajectory sampling/evaluation. Feasibility, comfort, efficiency, safety and selected rule compliance are evaluated separately; outcomes trade off scenario coverage and trajectory cost rather than identifying a universal best planner.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Kochdumper et al., Results of the 2023 CommonRoad Motion Planning Competition for Autonomous Vehicles, arXiv:2411.06425, Sections 0.2-0.5; particularly pp. 2-4 evaluation criteria and pp. 7-10 planner descriptions/results, opened full HTML paper.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Current motion-planning algorithm comparison in simulated highway/urban scenarios with interactive SUMO agents, a CommonRoad scenario set and a nonlinear single-track vehicle model; not a deployment comparison.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: primary comparative competition report on motion-planning algorithms
cell_disposition_register.inputs: CommonRoad road/scenario files, traffic participants (record-adapted or simulated), ego initial state and goal region, nonlinear single-track vehicle model, selected rules and a fixed evaluation/compute budget.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Feasible goal-reaching trajectories and benchmark measures for solved scenarios, collision/kinematic/road feasibility, jerk/comfort, obstacle distance, rule compliance and runtime under the competition protocol.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The competition uses its chosen model, scenario split, feasibility checker, cost weights, traffic simulation, two-core six-hour test budget and two submitted teams; the results compare those implementations only.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: A 2023 competition report posted in 2024 with only two final competing planners and bounded, mostly European benchmark scenarios; competition scores do not establish general algorithm ranking, public-road safety, regulatory acceptance or behavior under Nigerian traffic/road conditions.

relationship_evidence.explanation: The report contrasts a reachability-based decision module coupled to an optimization trajectory planner with a trajectory-sampling/evaluation planner; both target feasible goal-reaching trajectories but use different search/control representations under the same benchmark constraints. This is an evidenced alternative for the competition task, not equivalence for all ODDs.

remaining_scope: Finite-state/rule-based, graph/search, sampling, optimization, lattice, MPC, interactive prediction-planning, learned policies and RL; compare comfort, safety, feasibility, runtime and closed-loop evidence.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: Mapped a specific head-to-head competition comparison; broader rule/search/lattice/MPC/learned/RL methods, ODDs and independent road evidence remain open.

cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: The learned method models surrounding traffic for planner evaluation; it is not itself evidence that an ego planner is learned or deployed.

cell_disposition_register.inputs: Benchmark scenario, agent observations/state, traffic-agent policy and simulator transition model.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Non-ego agent actions/trajectories and resulting closed-loop planner evaluation traces or metrics.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The reported diversity and planner comparisons are for nuPlan-R's trained/reactive-agent setup and evaluation scenes, not evidence of real-road behavior or universally superior agents.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: Preprint, simulator and authors' reported metrics; no independent replication or operational safety claim.

relationship_evidence.explanation: Learned reactive agents are an alternative to rule-based IDM agents in the evaluation environment.

cell_disposition_register.claim: A concrete emerging end-to-end planning algorithm, World4Drive, combines a multi-modal trajectory-intention encoder with a spatial/semantic/temporal latent world model; it predicts intention-conditioned future latent states, scores candidate trajectories with a world-model selector, and is trained with self-supervised future-observation reconstruction plus trajectory supervision. The authors evaluate it on open-loop nuScenes and closed-loop NavSim; this is one research implementation, not a general world-model solution or road-validated planner.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Zheng et al., World4Drive, arXiv:2507.00603v1 (ICCV 2025), full 10-page paper: abstract and Section 1, PDF pp. 1-2, lines 7-23 and 60-97; method Sections 3.1-3.3, PDF pp. 2-4, lines 163-180 and 265-345; benchmarks/results Section 4, PDF pp. 4-6, lines 346-421; ablations PDF pp. 6-7, lines 422-460.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Emerging research algorithm documented in an ICCV 2025 paper, placed in the future/futuristic frontier cell because it represents a recently proposed end-to-end latent-world-model approach rather than established vehicle practice.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: end-to-end, intention-conditioned latent-world-model planning algorithm
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Multi-view RGB camera images; ego driving command and trajectory vocabulary; vision-language and metric-depth model priors for semantic/spatial encoding; temporal image context and candidate multimodal trajectories.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Candidate ego trajectories, predicted intention-conditioned future latent scene states, world-model scores and a selected planning trajectory; benchmark outputs include open-loop L2/collision metrics and closed-loop NavSim PDMS submetrics.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The paper uses selected nuScenes and NavSim benchmark protocols; the NavSim trajectory is interpolated using an LQR controller. Its method assumes useful pretrained depth/semantic priors, trajectory-intention vocabulary and benchmark-specific data/preprocessing; all reported comparisons are within the study's models and experimental setup.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: Single research paper and benchmark evaluation; no physical vehicle or public-road trials are reported. Open-loop displacement/collision metrics and closed-loop simulator scores do not establish safety, ODD coverage, robustness to distribution shift, regulatory acceptance or transfer to Nigerian traffic. The abstract and body differ slightly in the relative L2-error reduction (18.1% versus 18.2%); no percentage is repeated here. Code is stated as forthcoming in the inspected version.

relationship_evidence.explanation: This algorithm is one alternative to modular perception/prediction/planning and to other end-to-end trajectory-generation/world-model designs when they share the same sensor-to-ego-trajectory task; its benchmark interface and validation scope must be matched before comparing performance.

remaining_scope: Other independently inspected world-model and end-to-end planning alternatives, tool/code availability, independent replication, broader ODD and road-transfer evidence; separately inspect autonomous-racing methods and their transfer boundary.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: MAP056 is one item-level example, not saturation of the frontier cell. Continue with other method families and counter-searches; no public-road or safety claim is made.

cell_disposition_register.claim: NAVSIM is an emerging data-driven benchmark/tool that computes short-horizon BEV simulation metrics from logged real-world scenes without reacting other agents to the evaluated policy; its authors report better alignment with closed-loop scores than traditional displacement errors, while explicitly noting simulator domain gap and non-reactive limits.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Dauner et al., NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track, abstract and Sections 1, 3-4; PDF pp. 1-4, 8-10; lines 8-27 and 50-83 of the opened proceedings PDF for motivation, non-reactive protocol and reported correlation with closed-loop evaluation.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Emerging research benchmark and evaluation tool for learned driving/planning policies; it evaluates trajectories from recorded real-world scenes, but is not a fully interactive traffic simulator or road test.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: benchmark, dataset-evaluation tool and non-reactive simulator
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Logged sensor scenes and policy trajectory outputs over a selected short horizon, OpenScene/nuScenes-derived data, and BEV scene abstractions.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Short-horizon progress, time-to-collision, collision/map-compliance and aggregate benchmark metrics for policy comparison; the official evaluation server and research code are linked by authors.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The non-ego environment is held non-reactive during rollout; results reflect the sampled dataset, BEV abstraction, chosen metrics and benchmark split. The authors report correlation with closed-loop results, not equivalence.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: The paper identifies limited scale/cost of closed-loop tests and synthetic-sensor simulator domain gap as motivations. NAVSIM does not model policy-induced reactions by other agents and cannot establish on-road performance, complete ODD coverage or safety. Dataset licensing/provenance and current benchmark maintenance require separate verification.

cell_disposition_register.claim: A research foundation for safe learning-based control is to model the admissible state-dependent action set explicitly and parameterize policy updates so actions are sampled within it; convergence and hard-safety claims depend on known safe-action constraints, deterministic dynamics and stated policy/step-size assumptions. AISTATS 2024 validates the approach on simulated inverted-pendulum and quadcopter tasks, not a road vehicle.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Suttle et al., AISTATS 2024, PMLR 238, pp. 4420-4428: Section 2, pp. 2-3, safe set/action-set formulation and Assumptions 1-4; Section 3, pp. 4-6, constrained policy-gradient algorithm and convergence theorem; Section 4, pp. 6-8, simulated inverted-pendulum and quadcopter studies; conclusion p. 8. Full proceedings PDF: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v238/suttle24a/suttle24a.pdf.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Future/futuristic foundation candidate for the control/RL research frontier: foundational safe-policy-gradient concepts in nonlinear dynamical systems, adjacent to but not demonstrated on vehicle control. Horizon denotes the research direction, not adoption or transfer certainty.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: safe reinforcement-learning foundations for constrained policy-gradient control
cell_disposition_register.inputs: State and action spaces; deterministic system transition model; a known safe set and state-dependent set of actions that keep the next state safe; a differentiable parameterized stochastic policy; reward and step-size schedule; safety constraints such as CBF-derived action sets.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: A constrained policy-gradient update whose sampled actions remain in the specified admissible action set, with a theorem showing convergence to stationary points and hard-constraint satisfaction under the paper's assumptions; not a vehicle controller or road-safety certificate.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: Safe action sets are known and have positive, bounded measure; system transitions and policy distributions satisfy the paper's regularity/reachability assumptions; deterministic dynamics and valid safe-set characterization hold; update steps meet stated summability conditions.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: The paper leaves learning or approximating the safe-action set while preserving guarantees to future work. Demonstrations are simulation-only inverted-pendulum/quadcopter cases; no automotive model, vehicle experiment, road validation, safety case, independent reproduction or certification is established. Transfer to vehicle control requires vehicle-specific dynamics, ODD and safety-set validation.

relationship_evidence.explanation: This work complements the mapped racing LMPC and vehicle-specific safe-control studies by providing general constrained-RL foundations; its quadcopter results do not validate vehicle-control transfer or replace vehicle-specific evidence.

remaining_scope: Compare safe-RL formulations, learning-augmented MPC, differentiable control and autonomous-racing methods; establish vehicle-specific transfer, safe-set estimation, independent reproduction and physical validation, and distinguish racing demonstrations from road-certified control.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: One cross-domain safe-policy-gradient foundation is mapped with its non-vehicle simulation scope explicit; vehicle-specific foundations, alternatives and transfer evidence remain open.

cell_disposition_register.claim: An emerging shared-control safety-filter design learns a neural state-action safety value function from black-box interaction using model-free Hamilton-Jacobi reachability, then applies a Q-control-barrier-function constraint to minimally modify a human driver's requested action. cell_disposition_register.outputs: A minimally modified steering/braking command satisfying the learned Q-CBF safety constraint, with simulator feedback and operator-facing intervention cues.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The safety function is learned from black-box interactions and is valid for the defined action set, failure set and Silverstone/Assetto Corsa ODD. relationship_evidence.explanation: For shared-control safety filtering under the same defined ODD, Q-CBF HCSF is compared with a last-resort filter that intervenes at the safe-set boundary without minimizing deviation from human intent. The alternatives differ in intervention objective and human-control contract; neither is a substitute for the nominal trajectory-tracking controller or a universal ADS fallback.

cell_disposition_register.claim: Näke et al.'s emerging zonal E/E algorithm solves component-to-zone assignment and ZCU placement as a p-median/location-covering ILP, then routes harness nets via a capacitated multi-commodity-flow ILP minimizing total wire length. Optimality holds for the stated simplified graph and objective; one synthetic base-vehicle topology study excludes ZCU interconnects and detailed 3D feasibility. It is a distinct alternative to ConvIO's clustering/greedy algorithm, not a head-to-head comparison.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Näke et al., IEEE ITEC Asia-Pacific 2025, DOI 10.1109/ITECAsia-Pacific63742.2025.11345003; full paper Sections II-III (pp. 1-3) and IV-V (pp. 3-5): author-deposited PDF https://www.ifte.de/mitarbeiter/lienig/ITEC_AP_2025.pdf; TU Dresden peer-reviewed record https://fis.tu-dresden.de/portal/en/publications/efficient-architecture-evaluation-and-generation-of-automotive-wiring-harnesses(724c6c22-aba8-4b64-a244-932c01ab6a71).html.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Emerging 2025 research algorithm for early-stage zonal vehicle E/E architecture exploration; peer-reviewed publication does not establish OEM adoption or production-tool status.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: p-median zone-placement/component-assignment and capacitated multi-commodity-flow harness-routing ILP algorithms
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Simplified vehicle graph with component candidate nodes and routing edges/capacities; base point-to-point netlist; chosen number of ZCUs; wire cross-sectional areas and a wire-length minimization objective; Gurobi ILP solver in the reported experiment.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Exact model-optimal ZCU locations and component assignments for the given p-median formulation; per-net paths satisfying modeled edge-capacity constraints and minimizing total modeled wire length; runtime and harness-length comparison metrics.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The graph approximates feasible vehicle paths; netlist, edge capacities, wire areas and candidate ZCU positions adequately represent the design question; exactness is only relative to the stated ILP, objective and constraints.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: Single simplified base-vehicle topology and synthetic randomized point-to-point nets; no ZCU-to-ZCU wiring, 3D/circle-packing feasibility, detailed power/data/EMC/timing constraints, independent solver reproduction, production vehicle validation or safety evidence. Exact model optimum is not physical/global optimum. No head-to-head test against ConvIO or competing design tools.

relationship_evidence.explanation: MAP089 and MAP085 address comparable zonal placement/assignment and wiring-route design outputs. MAP089 uses exact p-median and multi-commodity-flow ILPs under explicit graph/capacity/length assumptions; MAP085 uses ConvIO's k-means/elbow, chassis-distance clustering and greedy route method. Neither paper is a head-to-head comparison and their objectives/constraints are not interchangeable.

remaining_scope: Additional zone-placement/partitioning and routing alternatives; implementation and independent reproduction; include ZCU-to-ZCU networks, power/data timing, 3D packaging, EMC, weight/cost and production constraints, plus cross-platform evidence.

Compare exact ILP methods with ConvIO and other clustering, heuristic and network-optimization approaches; do not infer adoption from peer-reviewed research or model optimality from a simplified graph.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: Two distinct zonal algorithm families are now mapped (ConvIO MAP085 and Näke et al. MAP089), with a conditional alternative relation and no head-to-head claim; other algorithms, physical constraints and independent validation remain open.

cell_disposition_register.claim: ConvIO's future-zonal design uses a distinct algorithmic stack: k-d-tree mapping of I/O to chassis connection points, k-means/elbow heuristic for initial zone count, Dijkstra-derived chassis path distances for hierarchical agglomerative refinement, and greedy nearest-neighbor communication-path generation. The paper tests this stack in one modeled BEV case; it does not prove globally optimal zoning or deployed network performance.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Mauser et al., IEEE Access 14 (2026), pp. 98616-98632, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3707952; full text Sections V.A-V.E and Algorithms 1-6 (PDF pp. 4-8), with validation and limitations in Sections VI-VIII. Full published text inspected at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/408232334_ConvIO_A_Framework_for_Convergence_of_Inputs_and_Outputs_in_Automotive_Zonal_EE_Architectures; metadata cross-checked at TUM institutional record.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Future/futuristic algorithm candidate for designing zonal SDV E/E integration; research implementation and one modeled case do not establish deployment or adoption.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: chassis-aware clustering and communication-route generation algorithm stack for zonal I/O integration
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Chassis graph, I/O and attachment locations, candidate number of zones, chosen clustering linkage, aggregator candidates, HPC location and selected bus/redundant/star-ring communication topology.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: I/O clusters/zones refined by chassis path distance and a generated communication tree/path set to the HPC; the paper compares total modeled cable length, not optimality guarantees or live-network QoS.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The chassis graph and I/O coordinates capture relevant geometry; heuristic-selected cluster count and linkage are suitable; the greedy routing output is an acceptable candidate for the modeled topology; objective prioritizes the reported cable-length comparison.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: The paper combines heuristics and a greedy route method; global optimality is not established. One BEV-model scenario, limited cable-length KPI and no independent implementation/reproduction; latency, network load, fault containment, cybersecurity, production routing constraints and cross-platform robustness are not validated.

relationship_evidence.explanation: MAP085 isolates the computational methods embedded within the broader ConvIO architecture-design framework mapped in MAP084; it is not an independent replication or a second architecture outcome.

remaining_scope: Compare ConvIO's chassis-aware clustering/routing heuristics with alternative zonal allocation, network optimization, service-oriented diagnostics and secure OTA integration methods; verify implementation, constraints, global/operational performance and deployment rather than inferring adoption from a research paper.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: One distinct algorithm stack from MAP084's framework is mapped; alternative methods, independent reproduction, optimality and production network validation remain open.

cell_disposition_register.claim: A foundational safety-V&V competency is recognizing that rare severe outcomes make direct road-exposure demonstrations statistically demanding: required miles depend on event rate, confidence/precision target and comparator assumptions, while underreporting and a moving human-driver benchmark add uncertainty. RAND's 2016 analysis concludes that driving alone cannot establish fatality/injury safety before release under its studied assumptions; it does not conclude that ADS safety is impossible to assess.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Kalra and Paddock, RAND RR-1478-RC (2016), official 15-page report: Executive Summary pp. 1-2; statistical formulations/results pp. 3-6; benchmark and limitation discussion. Full official RAND PDF opened 2026-10-26; TRID bibliographic record cross-checked.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Established foundational knowledge for planning ADS safety evidence and interpreting road-test claims; the report is a historical U.S. statistical analysis, not a current universal validation prescription.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: statistical safety-evidence foundation and test-adequacy limitation
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Event/failure definition and rate, exposure distance, desired confidence or precision, benchmark/comparator rate, reporting completeness and stated autonomy/ODD assumptions.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: An estimated exposure/sample requirement and an uncertainty-aware conclusion about what road-test data can establish under those assumptions; motivates combining evidence types rather than relying on road miles alone.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: RAND's numerical illustrations use U.S. historical human-driver data, rare-event statistical models, defined failure metrics and an explicitly scoped fully autonomous category; results change with vehicle class, ODD, comparator, event definition and assumptions.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: 2016 policy research, not a standard or regulator acceptance criterion. It does not establish today's crash rates, a universally required mileage threshold, scenario/simulator validity, causal safety improvement, or that simulation/other methods automatically solve residual uncertainty. U.S. rates and legal context do not transfer directly to Nigeria or other jurisdictions.

relationship_evidence.explanation: Road exposure contributes operational evidence but, under the report's rare-event assumptions, cannot alone supply timely pre-release statistical proof for severe outcomes; scenario, simulation, component and other evidence may complement it, but the report does not validate any particular substitute or fixed assurance sequence.

remaining_scope: ODD and system boundaries, hazards/risk, requirements traceability, scenario concepts, safety argument basics, statistical test adequacy and simulation/vehicle evidence limits.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: One bounded historical statistical-foundation claim is mapped; the cell is terminal as a candidate. Current evidence, statistical alternatives, scenario validity, safety-case fundamentals and jurisdictional context remain area-level saturation limits.

cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Component/system functional safety and SOTIF are related but non-identical safety workstreams.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: functional-safety and SOTIF standards scope distinction
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Item/system definition, intended functions, hazards, malfunction behavior, performance limits and reasonably foreseeable misuse context.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Separate engineering processes and evidence for E/E malfunction-related risk and SOTIF-related insufficiency/misuse risk.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: Claims are restricted to official public scope summaries; full licensed texts and program-specific editions were not inspected, and cybersecurity is not subsumed by ISO 21448.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: Standards are paid beyond preview and 21448 revision is underway; confirm edition/status and applicability before compliance decisions.

relationship_evidence.explanation: The standards address distinct hazard sources and can complement one another; neither alone is an ADS-wide safety case.

cell_disposition_register.claim: Compositional controller assurance requires explicit analytical behavior/safety specifications and an ODD, subsystem assume-guarantee contracts, and control-invariant safe sets; the CoCoSaFe study treats these as prerequisites for conditional code-level verification, not universal proof obligations or accepted certification criteria.

cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Future/futuristic foundation claim: formal prerequisites for a research-stage compositional controller-verification approach; it does not assert these are universally standardized competencies or regulator-mandated criteria.

cell_disposition_register.outputs: A structured set of assumptions, guarantees and modeled safe operating conditions that can support conditional subsystem reasoning and subsequent code verification; not a safety certificate or proof of complete ADS safety.

cell_disposition_register.limitations: The paper's formal foundations do not establish universal standardization, complete ADS coverage, real-world ODD adequacy, physical-road safety, tool qualification, certification acceptance or independent replication. remaining_scope: Compare formal-assurance foundations and alternatives across ODD/specification adequacy, compositional contracts, runtime monitoring, learned-component assurance, tool soundness/qualification and standards or regulator acceptance; distinguish research assumptions from normative requirements.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: One paper-grounded foundation claim is mapped as a prerequisite to MAP081. This does not close the future-foundations cell; compare alternative foundations and verify normative, tool and external-validity evidence.

cell_disposition_register.claim: An emerging operational-safety hazard-analysis method combines Event Sequence Diagrams, Concurrent Task Analysis, STPA and Fault Tree Analysis across system, scenario and hazard-identification stages to model interactions among L4 driverless ADS fleet vehicles, remote operators and operational personnel. Its published demonstration is a bounded MaaS fleet case, not a validated universal safety method or proof of risk reduction.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Correa-Jullian et al., full open-access SAGE article: abstract lines 29-32; method comparison Table 1 lines 107-120; operational case analysis and results at lines 315 onward and 620-647, including method-specific overlap and limited operational data.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Emerging research method published online in 2024 for operational safety of driverless L4 ADS-as-a-service fleets; maturity reflects a proposed integrated approach, not established universal practice.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: integrated operational hazard-identification and scenario-modeling methodology
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Fleet/ADS system boundary, agents and their functions/tasks, operational phases and scenarios, initiating events, control interactions, human-task dependencies, failure modes and available operational evidence.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Structured hazard scenarios/catalog, event sequences, interaction/task models, unsafe control actions, fault-tree contributors, responsibilities and candidate safety requirements or mitigations; models can inform but do not themselves complete quantitative risk assessment.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: The paper's ESD, CoTA, STPA and FTA descriptions and its single L4 MaaS case support a contextual method claim. Different system scope, operational phases, expertise and data can change the methods' relative contribution and outputs.
cell_disposition_register.limitations: One on-route passenger phase of a modeled driverless L4 MaaS fleet; the study reports that only 13% of failure modes were identified by all three compared methods, with method-specific unique contributions, and warns results depend on analysis. Limited operational data constrained risk quantification. No field effectiveness, complete safety case, comparative universal superiority or reduction in actual incidents is established.

relationship_evidence.explanation: ESD/FTA represent event sequences and causal combinations, while CoTA/STPA address task and control interactions; the paper combines them because their modeled aspects differ, not because every ADS requires this exact stack or order.

remaining_scope: ISO 26262/SOTIF safety engineering, hazard/risk analysis, scenario-based testing, coverage/metrics, fault injection, MIL/SIL/HIL/XIL, closed-course/on-road validation and safety cases; compare evidence strength and assumptions.

cell_disposition_register.claim: ScenicProver is a research-stage compositional assurance method for learning-enabled cyber-physical systems: it combines assume-guarantee contracts, simulation-based probabilistic evidence, user-supplied formal proofs and imported assumptions, then composes evidence into system-level guarantees and a provenance-tracked assurance case. Its AEB case study uses assumed sensor guarantees and simplified physics; the authors explicitly leave sim-to-real validity to future work.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Vin et al., ScenicProver, arXiv:2511.02164v1 (2025), full HTML: abstract and framework scope lines 45-85; evidence assumptions and sim-to-real statement §4.1 lines 184-211; combined contract evidence/assurance case §5; AEB case study §6; generated assurance-case examples Appendix 0.C.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Research frontier for composing heterogeneous formal, probabilistic and assumed evidence over learning-enabled ADS components; the horizon reflects a preprint/tool-framework example, not accepted certification practice.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: compositional probabilistic assume-guarantee safety-assurance method
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Component interfaces and contracts, Scenic scenario distributions/simulator traces, independently generated proof results, imported external assumptions and confidence levels.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Sound lower bounds on contract-satisfaction probabilities under stated independence and modeling assumptions; composed system-level contracts and an assurance case with evidence provenance.
cell_disposition_register.assumptions: Component contracts and interface model are valid; evidence-generation independence conditions hold; simulator distribution represents the modeled environment; imported manufacturer guarantees and supplied proofs are correct and applicable. The AEB case study also uses simplified physics.
limitations: Preprint submitted to TACAS 2026; research framework, not a deployed vehicle or regulator-approved safety-case process.

AEB demonstration is a simplified simulation case, relying on manufacturer sensor guarantees, supplied Lean proofs and stated model assumptions; the authors explicitly leave the sim-to-real gap unresolved.
No complete-vehicle road validation, independent replication, normative acceptance, or proof that all relevant hazards/ODD conditions are captured.

relationship_evidence.explanation: Compositional contract evidence can organize test, proof and external-assumption results alongside safety cases and scenario validation; it does not replace safety engineering, independent evidence review or physical/operational validation.

remaining_scope: Compare with CoCoSaFe, AMLAS, UL 4600 safety-case practice, monolithic statistical testing and runtime-monitor/assurance alternatives.
Assess evidence dependence, assumption provenance, distribution shift, ODD completeness, model validity, tool qualification and real-vehicle transfer.
cell_disposition_register.review_note: One research-stage method is mapped; this does not establish accepted assurance practice or close the future-method family/task.

The front-matter suggested citation has a title mismatch, so claims use the report title/number and inspected technical sections only.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Established/traditional ADS test-design technique documented in a 2018 U.S. government-sponsored preliminary framework; it is not a binding requirement, complete standard or evidence of current field practice.

cell_disposition_register.inputs: Selected ADS feature and intended ODD, OEDR capabilities/behaviors, tactical maneuvers, expected objects/events, failure modes and mitigation strategies, facilities/personnel, data collection plan and performance/success metrics.

remaining_scope: ISO 26262/SOTIF safety engineering, hazard/risk analysis, scenario-based testing, coverage/metrics, fault injection, MIL/SIL/HIL/XIL, closed-course/on-road validation and safety cases; compare evidence strength and assumptions.

cell_disposition_register.claim: CoCoSaFe is a research-stage, offline code-level controller-verification method: it formalizes a controller ODD and analytical safety specification, decomposes them with assume-guarantee contracts and control-invariant safe sets, then applies bounded model checking to traditional controller code and a BMC/neural-verifier decomposition to DNN controllers. Its published ACC/LKA case studies do not establish full-ADS assurance, road validation or certification acceptance.
cell_disposition_register.exact_locator: Nenchev et al., Journal of Systems and Software 230 (2025), 112499, published version, CC-BY 2.5 at White Rose Research Online: Sections 4.1-4.3.2 (PDF pp. 3-8) for formalization, compositional contracts, invariant sets, BMC and DNN-verifier decomposition; Section 5 (pp. 8-10) for seven ACC/LKA controller implementations; Section 6 (pp. 11-12) for threats to validity and stated future extensions; DOI 10.1016/j.jss.2025.112499.
cell_disposition_register.area_horizon_context: Future/futuristic frontier candidate because this peer-reviewed 2025 framework remains a research method with bounded ACC/LKA case studies and authors identify urban/other-controller expansion as future work; the horizon denotes research maturity, not a prediction of acceptance or deployment.
cell_disposition_register.item_type: compositional formal code-verification technique for safety-relevant ADAS controller implementations
cell_disposition_register.inputs: Controller implementation/code; formally specified desired longitudinal/lateral behavior and safety requirements; analytical environment/dynamics model and ODD; subsystem assumptions/contracts and computed control-invariant safe sets; BMC bound and, for DNN controllers, a neural-network verifier such as Marabou.
cell_disposition_register.outputs: Offline verification or falsification result for controller code over the modeled safe set/ODD under the specified contracts and tool assumptions; the paper reports seven ACC/LKA controller types analyzed in minutes on a workstation. source_additions.supported_claim: ConvIO proposes a five-step zonal I/O convergence method combining graph-based I/O/chassis mapping, k-means/elbow zone-count selection, routing-aware hierarchical clustering, zonal aggregator placement and communication-path generation. source_additions.claim_limit: Single modeled vehicle case; cross-platform and production generalization is explicitly unproven. Cable length is the main quantified outcome. The article identifies additional constraints/KPIs, powernet integration and functional-safety fault-containment as future work; no production deployment, complete safety/security architecture, vehicle test campaign or independent replication is established.
source_additions.credibility_assessment: Peer-reviewed primary article; full published text was inspectable via author-uploaded public copy and metadata was cross-checked with the TUM institutional record. Method and reported results are author-evaluated; repository/source code was not independently built and results were not independently reproduced.
source_additions.relationship_context: A physical E/E architecture-design method complementary to software/middleware/interface design. It does not define runtime service APIs or establish a universally optimal zonal architecture, safety case or production implementation.

source_additions.supported_claim: The authors formulate zonal-control-unit placement/component assignment as a p-median/location-covering ILP and harness routing as a capacitated multi-commodity-flow ILP, yielding exact optimal solutions for the stated simplified graph, objective and constraints. A synthetic single-vehicle-topology experiment uses randomly generated point-to-point nets, reports runtime scaling and shorter wire-length metrics as zone count rises, and explicitly omits ZCU interconnects and detailed geometric feasibility.
source_additions.claim_limit: Exactness is conditional on the simplified graph/model, objective and constraints, not physical/global optimality of a complete production vehicle harness. Synthetic netlists, one base vehicle graph, no ZCU-to-ZCU wiring, no circle-packing/3D feasibility and Gurobi implementation limit external validity. Reported wire-length trends do not establish OEM adoption, safety, signal timing, power integrity, electromagnetic compatibility or production cost outcomes. The paper itself identifies multiobjective and additional physical constraints as future work.
source_additions.credibility_assessment: Peer-reviewed primary conference paper with complete author-deposited text and institutional metadata. Technical claims are limited to paper-described formulation and experiments; no external code, data, solver file or independent reproduction was inspected.
source_additions.relationship_context: A comparable zonal assignment/routing task to ConvIO MAP084/MAP085, but an alternative optimization formulation: p-median plus exact ILP routing under an explicit simplified graph and length/capacity objective, rather than ConvIO's reported clustering heuristics and greedy route generation. Outputs and assumptions are not interchangeable.

source_additions.publisher_or_author: Xingyu Zhao, Robab Aghazadeh-Chakherlou, Chih-Hong Cheng, Peter Popov and Lorenzo Strigini; arXiv / ITSC 2025
source_additions.title: On the Need for a Statistical Foundation in Scenario-Based Testing of Autonomous Vehicles
source_additions.source_family_type: primary research paper; arXiv full-text record, accepted by ITSC 2025 per record
source_additions.evidence_layer: statistical adequacy, stopping rules, residual risk and simulation-to-real alignment in scenario-based testing
source_additions.publication_version_status: ITSC 2025 peer-reviewed paper; Warwick WRAP accepted manuscript under CC BY 4.0 opened 2026-10-29. Repository record dates formal publication 2026-03-16.
source_additions.access_level: Full 9-page Warwick author-accepted manuscript opened and inspected, including statistical models, simulated-versus-road fidelity proposal, examples and limitations; repository explicitly warns it may differ from version of record.
source_additions.precise_locator: Warwick WRAP accepted PDF https://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/id/eprint/191927/7/WRAP-need-statistical-foundation-2025.pdf: Introduction pp. 1-2 (four open questions); metric and estimation models pp. 4-6; Risk Estimation Fidelity (REF) definition/workflow and numerical example pp. 6-8; limitations and conclusion p. 8. Bibliographic/version record https://wrap.warwick.ac.uk/id/eprint/191927/.
source_additions.supported_claim: The paper distinguishes directed scenario testing from operational-profile/mile-based testing and argues neither universally dominates: targeted tests can find defects efficiently but may overweight operationally rare faults, while operational testing estimates frequency under its sampled profile. It proposes proof-of-concept probability-of-failure-per-scenario models and Risk Estimation Fidelity, comparing real and synthetic risk estimates with a predefined tolerance/confidence and treating residual risk, stopping rules, debugging effectiveness and simulator bias as linked questions.
source_additions.claim_limit: The manuscript explicitly presents proof-of-concept models, simplified failure-region assumptions and illustrative data; REF is a proposed statistical comparison, not a regulator-certified simulator qualification or demonstrated general transfer guarantee. Normal approximations may fail for rare events, operational-profile representativeness and real/synthetic comparability remain assumptions, and the accepted manuscript may differ from the version of record.
source_additions.credibility_assessment: Peer-reviewed ITSC 2025 primary research, full author-accepted manuscript hosted in the University of Warwick repository under CC BY 4.0; bibliographic status cross-checked against the repository record. Supports model/method description and its stated limits, not validation of deployment claims.
source_additions.relationship_context: Statistical scenario evidence complements road exposure and simulation validation; neither replaces the other without context-specific assumptions and transfer evidence.

source_additions.supported_claim: GUARD uses Gaussian Processes and level-set sampling to adaptively estimate safe, unsafe and unknown regions in continuous parameterized scenario spaces; it balances uncertainty exploration with sampling near the pass/fail boundary. Its authors evaluate it against selected baselines on ten five-parameter simulated scenarios, using a single minimum-distance threshold, repeated trials and estimated coverage/accuracy metrics; the authors state that single-metric and discrete-parameter limits remain and simulator sim-to-real fidelity is an open problem.
source_additions.claim_limit: Evidence is confined to the paper's chosen simulated scenarios, planner, five continuous parameters and single thresholded safety measure; it does not prove completeness of the ODD/scenario set, calibration of the simulator, physical-road safety, universal stopping criteria, regulatory acceptance or certification. Categorical scenario parameters and multi-metric safety are identified as limitations.
source_additions.credibility_assessment: Full primary paper in the peer-reviewed CoRL Proceedings of Machine Learning Research; directly inspected methods, benchmark design, reported results and limitations. Author-reported benchmark performance is not independent reproduction or real-world validation.
source_additions.relationship_context: Coverage-driven scenario generation complements hazard analysis and statistical adequacy; it does not prove that the scenario distribution or operational domain is complete.

source_additions.supported_claim: The paper estimates accident/low-TTC probability under a base distribution of standard traffic behavior by learning a cross-entropy importance-sampling distribution that generates failures more frequently and applying likelihood-ratio weights. source_additions.credibility_assessment: Full primary paper in the peer-reviewed NeurIPS proceedings; method and experiment details directly inspected. Reported performance is author-evaluated and has not been independently reproduced here.
source_additions.relationship_context: Rare-event importance sampling can complement road exposure and coverage-based testing by estimating a probability under a stated operational base distribution; it is not interchangeable with scenario coverage or physical validation.

source_additions.publisher_or_author: Trey P. Weber, Rajan K. Aggarwal and J. Christian Gerdes; IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles
source_additions.title: Human-Inspired Autonomous Racing in Low Friction Environments
source_additions.source_family_type: peer-reviewed primary research article; full article text hosted on ResearchGate and bibliographic record cross-checked with IEEE Xplore
source_additions.evidence_layer: Nonlinear MPC planning/control with coupled lateral-longitudinal vehicle dynamics and high-slip tire behavior; physical snow/ice track experiment
source_additions.publication_version_status: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles, volume 10, issue 6, pages 3684-3696 (June 2025); DOI publication record cross-checked on IEEE Xplore; full text inspected 2026-10-29.
source_additions.access_level: Full 13-page article text inspected on ResearchGate (public full-text copy, CC BY 4.0 indicated); IEEE Xplore metadata/abstract cross-checked, but publisher full text was not directly accessible.
source_additions.precise_locator: Article pp. 3684-3696: Sections II-III compare professional-driver/baseline state and input use and specify the coupled high-slip vehicle/tire model; Sections V-A/B simulate and compare four NMPC formulations; Section VI and Figs. 10-15 report the full-scale 2018 VW Golf GTI snow/ice track experiment and disturbance response; Section VII compares behavior and states test-repeatability/transfer limits; conclusion discusses future collision-avoidance objectives.
source_additions.supported_claim: The authors formulate an online nonlinear MPC motion-planning/control framework with coupled lateral-longitudinal dynamics and a combined-slip tire model, then test it on one full-scale VW Golf GTI on a 1.4 km winter handling track with reported friction varying around 0.2-0.3. The article reports a snow-bank yaw disturbance response and a mean online solve time of 31 ms. For physical testing, the friction coefficient was treated as constant and estimated a priori from another experiment; varying surface conditions prevented repeatable physical lap-time comparisons, and the authors identify friction uncertainty and collision-avoidance objectives as future work.
source_additions.claim_limit: One research vehicle and racing/handling-track ODD, not public-road traffic, passenger comfort, collision avoidance or production validation. A single physical test campaign with varying grip does not independently validate safety or generalize to other vehicles/surfaces. The constant-friction assumption produces documented force-model mismatch; no complete friction estimator, repeatable comparative physical trial, safety certification or independent reproduction is established.
source_additions.credibility_assessment: Peer-reviewed IEEE journal article; complete article text and detailed experimental/model sections were inspected through a third-party full-text host, with bibliographic identity checked against IEEE Xplore. Host provenance is not the publisher copy, and the experiment/results remain author-reported rather than independently reproduced.
source_additions.relationship_context: Adds a physical low-friction alternative to simulation-only robust/adaptive methods and a concrete controller-to-vehicle validation case; it complements, but does not replace, low-grip estimation, target-vehicle HIL/road validation, fault/degraded-mode testing or ADS safety evidence.

source_additions.publisher_or_author: John K. Subosits and J. Christian Gerdes; IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles
source_additions.title: Impacts of Model Fidelity on Trajectory Optimization for Autonomous Vehicles in Extreme Maneuvers
source_additions.source_family_type: peer-reviewed primary research article; full accepted-manuscript text hosted on ResearchGate and bibliographic record/abstract cross-checked with IEEE Xplore
source_additions.evidence_layer: Trajectory-optimization model fidelity and physical tracking across ice, wet asphalt and dry asphalt
source_additions.publication_version_status: IEEE Transactions on Intelligent Vehicles 6(3), 546-558 (2021); DOI 10.1109/TIV.2021.3051325. IEEE Xplore confirms title, authors, journal, pages, publication date and abstract. Full article text inspected 2026-10-29.
source_additions.access_level: IEEE Xplore metadata and abstract inspected; complete 13-page accepted-manuscript text inspected on ResearchGate, which displays CC BY 4.0. Publisher full-text retrieval was blocked by JavaScript/robot verification; the inspected copy states it is accepted but not fully edited.
source_additions.precise_locator: Subosits and Gerdes, Sections II-IV for point-mass, single-track, constrained double-track and free double-track model assumptions and trajectory optimization; Section V and Table I for full-scale 2019 Volkswagen GTI trajectory tests on ice, wet asphalt and dry asphalt; pp. 10-11 / Fig. 11 for point-mass tracking yaw transient on ice; Conclusions for model-fidelity tradeoffs.
source_additions.supported_claim: The authors compare trajectories optimized with four models of increasing vehicle-dynamics fidelity and test them on a full-size automated Volkswagen GTI across ice, wet asphalt and dry asphalt. On the icy handling track, the point-mass-derived trajectory produced a high-sideslip pendulum transient while the vehicle negotiated linked corners; the higher-fidelity models better captured transient yaw and wheel-level friction limits in that case. The article's overall conclusion is conditional: more complex models can give a more nuanced view of limits and actuator coordination, but fidelity effects and performance vary by surface and objective, rather than establishing that the most complex model always wins.
source_additions.claim_limit: One 2019 VW GTI experiment in extreme-maneuver/handling-track conditions, not public-road ADS operation. The paper's physical results are author-reported and not independently reproduced; fitted vehicle/surface models and race-track objectives do not establish general controller superiority, road safety, fault tolerance, another vehicle's model validity or transfer to an operational ODD.
source_additions.credibility_assessment: Peer-reviewed IEEE journal publication with publisher-indexed metadata and abstract; full experimental sections and tables were inspected in a third-party-hosted accepted-manuscript copy. The version-of-record full text was not directly retrieved, and no independent reproduction was located in this review.
source_additions.relationship_context: Adds a physically tested model-fidelity comparison to the Control alternatives and to V&V evidence-quality review. Its surface-specific result cautions against both point-mass sufficiency claims and a universal more-fidelity-is-better rule; it does not replace target-vehicle validation, state-estimation/fault evidence or public-road safety evidence.

source_additions.publisher_or_author: Zhaohui Liang, Hang Zhou, Heye Huang and Xiaopeng Li; University of Wisconsin-Madison
source_additions.title: High-Slip-Ratio Control for Peak Tire-Road Friction Estimation Using Automated Vehicles
source_additions.source_family_type: primary research preprint; full arXiv HTML paper inspected
source_additions.evidence_layer: Active high-slip excitation, tire-road friction estimation, constrained longitudinal control, and limited real-vehicle field evaluation
source_additions.publication_version_status: arXiv:2603.09073v1 [cs.RO], submitted 2026-03-10; the inspected arXiv record identifies this as version 1, not a peer-reviewed version of record.
source_additions.access_level: Full paper inspected directly in arXiv HTML, including method, simulation and field-testing sections; open author preprint, not independently replicated.
source_additions.precise_locator: Sections II-C to II-E: simplified Magic Formula, locally fitted friction estimator, repeated-location variance aggregation, and constrained high-slip optimal-control formulation; Sections III-A/B: MATLAB/Simulink car-following simulation; Section III-C: real-world validation on a designated dry-concrete road with repeated autonomous-vehicle runs and offline estimation; Section IV: stated future validation across diverse surfaces and long-term operation.
source_additions.supported_claim: The preprint proposes an active longitudinal-friction estimation alternative: a constrained optimal controller deliberately generates high-slip measurements, locally fits a simplified Magic Formula, and aggregates repeated observations by location. It reports both closed-loop car-following simulation and repeated runs by one control-by-wire AV on a designated dry-concrete road; the field estimates are computed offline. Its safety constraints use modeled preceding/following vehicles in simulation, not interacting real traffic in the field trial.
source_additions.claim_limit: Version 1 preprint, one AV and one reported dry-concrete test stretch; the complete paper does not report cross-surface or multi-vehicle validation, an independent reference friction instrument/ground-truth comparison, real-traffic safety testing, or online onboard estimator deployment. The modeled car-following safety result is not a road-safety case, ADS approval, or proof that intentional high-slip excitation is safe for general traffic/ODDs.
source_additions.credibility_assessment: Primary author preprint with complete method and experiment sections directly inspected on arXiv; not peer reviewed in the version inspected. The real-vehicle experiments strengthen evidence beyond simulation, but the single-surface, single-platform scope and absence of independent replication/reference measurement materially limit confidence and transfer.
source_additions.relationship_context: Adds a contrasting active-excitation estimator to Control's passive/model-based friction foundations and a physical-testing counterexample for Safety V&V. It narrows whether real-vehicle friction-estimation trials exist, but the experimental surface and safety evidence remain bounded; it complements rather than closes the existing transfer and safety gaps.

source_enrichments.supported_claim: R157 Revision 1 is a consolidated 01-series text dated 27 March 2025, distinct from the original 00 series. Its indexed Annex 4 and sections 5-7 extracts prescribe a mix of mandatory and recommended ALKS scenarios, duration conditions for public-road testing (including at least five hours in heavily congested conditions and, when applicable, ten hours in free-flow conditions, subject to the stated sufficiency alternatives), and minimum data channels. The separate 7 October 2024 Revision 1 Amendment 2 search extract updates paragraph 5.1.7 on electromagnetic immunity by reference to UN R10. source_enrichments.claim_limit: The Revision 1 PDF and later amendment documents could not be opened directly (HTTP 403); the 2025 Revision 1 text is available here through official UNECE search-index extraction, not page-by-page direct inspection. UNTC lists Nigeria's application of original R157 effective 22 January 2021 but does not prove application of each later supplement domestically. source_enrichments.credibility_assessment: Primary UNECE and UNTC records support document identity, dated revision/amendment status, extracted operative test provisions, notification chronology and Nigeria's original application; direct full-text verification of the latest supplement chain remains incomplete.
source_enrichments.relationship_context: Regulatory transition/MRM evidence connects vehicle control, actuation/interface, driver handover and safety verification, but does not imply that an arbitrary stop or controller fault response satisfies R157 or constitutes a general ADS safe fallback.
