One full experimental tire-allocation study and bounded fault-control abstracts illustrate research and HIL alternatives without establishing universal fallback behavior.
query_log.limits: The Stanford experiment is one flat-surface racing line and estimates friction; tire-force utilization is calculated from commands and its force-to-torque mapping ignores wheel-slip dynamics. Autoware pages are implementation/design documentation and some are PR snapshots; no target vehicle calibration or certification. UCL paper full text timed out and SAGE full text is paywalled. Fault-control and ABS examples do not establish cross-actuator or public-road safety. No universal tire model, friction estimator, safe envelope or fallback is asserted.

Opened the complete 13-page PMLR CoRL 2023 Tu et al. GUARD paper: GP/level-set coverage partitions continuous scenario space into pass/fail/unknown; experiments use ten logical scenarios, five continuous parameters, a minimum-distance threshold, a selected planner and simulated testing; categorical/multiple metrics and sim-to-real fidelity remain limitations.

Opened the complete 9-page Warwick author-accepted Zhao et al. ITSC 2025 manuscript under CC BY 4.0: compares directed scenario and operational-profile testing, defines a proof-of-concept per-scenario failure probability, proposes Risk Estimation Fidelity (REF), and details assumptions and limitations; accepted manuscript may differ from version of record.
Cross-checked these distinct purposes against the previously opened full RAND RR-1478 road-exposure analysis; no universal ranking or replacement of physical/road evidence follows.
query_log.findings: The three method classes answer different questions: importance sampling deliberately shifts simulated traffic toward rare failures and uses likelihood ratios to estimate probability under a stated base distribution; GUARD estimates pass/fail/unknown regions over a selected parameterized scenario space to guide test selection and coverage; Zhao et al. connect targeted debugging and operational-profile acceptance through proof-of-concept pfs/REF models and expose residual-risk, stopping-rule and transfer assumptions. RAND road exposure remains a separate operational evidence path. Better sampling efficiency or high parameter-space coverage alone does not show that the operational distribution, ODD/scenario set, safety metric or simulator is complete or valid.
query_log.limits: O'Kelly's acceleration results are for a 2018 modeled California I-80 highway scenario and depend on an estimated base behavior distribution and simulator. GUARD's benchmark is ten simulated scenarios with five continuous variables, one thresholded metric and no independent physical validation; authors identify categorical/multiple-metric and sim-to-real limits. Zhao et al. label their models proof-of-concept and describe simplifications/rare-event statistical limitations; REF is not a regulator-certified qualification. No open-ended literature saturation, independent reproduction, local Nigerian ODD validation or physical ADS evidence is established.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds system-interface context from actuator management converting motion-control requests to steering/powertrain/brake targets and reporting degraded steering availability, plus a method requiring yaw-moment torque-vectoring actuation under steering fault.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: These are modeled study architectures, not general message/API or vehicle-network standards. No deployed timing, diagnostic, security, status schema or real-vehicle compatibility is established.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Complements the normalized-to-platform adaptation claim; cross-platform contracts and deployed degraded-mode alternatives remain open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds complementary evidence types: simulated fault injection with path/TTC/PET metrics, simulated fault-tolerant steering methods, and ALKS-regulation transition/MRM assessment excerpts. The records explicitly distinguish a test method, controller design and bounded type-approval framework.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Research articles were accessed through indexed excerpts; R157 current Revision 1 was inaccessible. Scenario-specific metrics, simulation results and scoped ALKS clauses do not establish broad ODD coverage, simulation validity, universal approval or ADS safety.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Strengthens one V&V-method cell's alternative evidence; full-text appraisal, simulator validity and independent physical/test evidence remain open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds one simulation toolchain/test design that couples planner, motion controller, actuators and vehicle dynamics for injected steering degradation, then assesses path deviation with TTC/PET over varied traffic initial conditions.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Publisher-indexed excerpts only; one model/fault/scenario family, five ego cases and scenario-derived thresholds. No independent fidelity validation, physical/on-road correlation, broad coverage or tool qualification is shown.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Provides an implementation example, not evidence that this toolchain or metric set is sufficient for ADS safety V&V.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds a full-text matched-design MPC versus robust H-infinity path-tracking comparison across three simulated road/friction scenarios; reported method trade-offs are scenario-dependent.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Simplified single-track linear-tire model and CarSim-Simulink simulation only; no comfort result, independent replication, physical-road validation, production ADS safety claim or universal winner.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Supports the existing mapped alternatives claim without adding a duplicate cell mapping.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds a full-text matched-tuning comparison of LQR, model-free and speed-adaptive model-free control, PID and nonlinear MPC, with accuracy/stability/comfort metrics, simulation and instrumented-vehicle tests.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: One platform and selected trajectories; no production ADS safety, broad ODD transfer or universal ranking. Publisher direct page was blocked; the full author manuscript was inspected.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Supports the existing alternative-method mapping and task disposition without adding a duplicate cell claim.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds directly inspected current academic and professional-learning examples to the existing standards/context mapping; Michigan states its fee, workload, CEU and badge, while Glasgow lists its 2026-27 credit-bearing guidance/planning course and entry requirements.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Two examples do not establish exhaustive curriculum or credential coverage, delivery/outcomes, professional recognition or legal requirements. COREN primary pages were inaccessible; no Nigerian credential conclusion is inferred.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: This is evidence for the existing current cell, not a new mapping claim or approved learner-sequence edge.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds directly inspected AUTOSAR Classic, Adaptive and Timing/Tracing curriculum references to the existing current AUTOSAR standards mapping, with their voluntary-use status and concrete integration/timing learning objectives.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Curriculum references are not courses, credentials or proof of provider delivery. The landing-page date and PDF 11-2026 filename suffix are inconsistent as of the review date; version chronology is unresolved.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Supports the current standards/resources cell without adding a duplicate standard claim or a mandatory education path.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds NVIDIA DriveWorks sensor abstraction, CAN and VehicleIO SDK documentation as a version-bounded vendor tool family, complementing the existing stack and HIL/SIL examples.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: API detail is archived 6.0.x; current API compatibility, target-hardware execution, vehicle deployment, end-to-end timing and safety/security assurance were not tested or inferred.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds evidence to the existing tools/current candidate; no new mapping or tool recommendation is created.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds full-text experimental tire-force/actuator-feasibility evidence and official implementation-level model, delay, steering-rate and command-gating constraints to the current foundation candidate.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: One bounded flat-surface research vehicle study; wheel-slip dynamics omitted and friction utilization calculated from commanded forces. Autoware settings are implementation documentation, not validated universal limits or safety certification.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Supports the existing current foundation claim without adding a mapping or generalizing specific parameter values to other vehicles.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds concrete current examples for QoS endpoint mismatch/deadline/liveliness signaling, explicit middleware identity/permissions activation, standardized recoverable transport-fault reporting, and implementation-specific command-heartbeat/emergency-timeout supervision. These complement the existing message/frame/timing/status contract claim.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: ROS Rolling is mutable; AUTOSAR platform requirements and Autoware parameters do not prove a particular vehicle's configuration, end-to-end deadlines, attack resistance, fault coverage, safe response or certification.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Supports the mapped foundation claim and bounded Integration foundation task only; does not establish a universal middleware, security architecture or fallback policy.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Official UNECE Revision 1 (27 March 2025) indexed text now supplies ALKS scenario and public-road test-duration/data-channel requirements, distinct from generic control fallback evidence; UNTC records notifications through January 2026 and Nigeria's original 2021 application.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Revision 1 and later amendment PDFs remain direct-fetch blocked; indexed text is not page-by-page clause verification. Later 00/01-series supplements and Nigeria's application of them remain unverified; this does not authorize higher-level ADS operation or establish a general safe fallback.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Version/status context only; no controller choice, safe fallback or R157 conformity conclusion is inferred.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Official UNECE Revision 1 indexed clauses add series-specific ALKS scenario and road-test requirements to the regulatory context for controller/interface handoffs, distinct from generic vehicle adapters and software fallback design.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Full clause-level inspection, applicable later series/supplements for a vehicle, domestic transposition and target-vehicle command/status contracts remain unverified.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Contextual source update only; no interface standard or system safety behavior is inferred.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Official UNECE Revision 1 indexed text (27 March 2025) exposes mandatory/recommended ALKS scenario coverage, public-road test-duration sufficiency conditions and minimum recorded channels; Amendment 2 separately updates electromagnetic immunity. This is bounded type-approval evidence, not a general ADS safety case.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Official PDFs remain direct-fetch blocked, so indexed excerpts are not page-by-page verified. Later 00/01-series supplements and Nigeria's application of them remain unestablished. No general ADS approval or Nigerian authorization claim is made.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Strengthens regulatory version traceability but leaves the exact current test clauses and wider Safety/V&V alternatives open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Official UNECE indexed Revision 1 text (27 March 2025) provides series-specific mandatory/recommended ALKS test scenarios, public-road test duration and minimum data channels; the separate Amendment 2 excerpt updates paragraph 5.1.7 by reference to UN R10.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Direct PDF retrieval is HTTP 403, so indexed extracts are not page-by-page verified. Later 00/01-series supplement clauses and Nigeria's application of those supplements remain unverified; R157 does not establish general ADS authorization or safety-case completeness.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds current-version evidence to the mapped regulatory-framework claim but leaves task and area saturation open for later supplement, jurisdiction, safety-case alternative and physical-validation review.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Full author manuscript reports hybrid kinematic-dynamic sideslip estimation and friction-change classification on a 4WD prototype across dry/wet asphalt and snow; 11% of friction changes were missed when vehicle excitation was insufficient.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Single prototype/study, author-reported results and no independent replication; not a universal low-grip capability or safe fallback. The missed-transition condition makes observability/excitation limits explicit.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a measurable, source-located state-estimation and low-adhesion boundary to the mapped foundation claim; does not close other vehicle-model or control-saturation gaps.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: SAE abstract describes an MPC constrained by a yaw-rate/centroid-sideslip phase-plane steady-state region under extreme adhesion conditions and reports two field-test scenarios.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Full paper unavailable; vehicle, protocol, baseline, metrics, outcome and limitations are unverified. Two scenarios do not establish general effectiveness or safety.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds an abstract-level low-grip MPC alternative without ranking it or representing publisher abstract evidence as a complete field-validation review.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Full NHTSA-sponsored paper documents HIL using real truck brake hardware and production stability-control ECUs, with TruckSim outputs compared to ramp-steer track tests; ABS/RSC thresholds were within about 1 mph while ESC results diverged with different driver throttle behavior.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Heavy-truck ESC/RSC evidence from 2009, not ADS or universal HIL qualification. Paper identifies model, tire/suspension/compliance and driver-behavior discrepancy; no transfer to the target vehicle is established.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a concrete physical-correlation/tool-fidelity example and its failure boundary; independent fidelity and target-vehicle validation remain open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The NHTSA HIL case correlates modeled scenarios with track maneuvers and real hardware, while reporting scenario-dependent ESC differences when driver behavior diverged; this is a bounded example of simulation-to-physical validation, not a whole-ADS safety case.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Heavy-truck stability-control scope and 2009 methods; does not establish simulator validity for another stack, full ODD/fault coverage, ADS safety effectiveness or approval.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a primary-source example of validation evidence and model discrepancy while preserving the broader Safety/V&V residuals.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Official FRSC sources independently list 2004/2012/2016 reviewed vintages and distinguish NRTR 2012 from its 2016 speed-limiter amendment, adding a narrowly located Nigerian road-rule example for planning context.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Compendium and implementation-document extracts are not a consolidated legal text; exact current legal status and additional amendments are unresolved. Speed-limiter provisions are not ADS-specific.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Improves local provenance and version specificity without turning agency summaries into operative law or ADS authorization.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: FRSC records differ by context: the 2024 compendium labels NRTR 2004/2012/2016 as reviewed, the RTSSS portal cites 2004 section 115 as scheme origin, and the 2025 post refers to NRTR (2024) without identifying a Gazette. These are agency statements, not a resolved legal-version chain.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: The RTSSS page and PDF extracts were not directly page-verified; no authenticated 2024 instrument, consolidated law, legal commencement, or Nigerian ADS authorization was established.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Makes the conflict and source-type limits visible in the mapped regulatory cell; legal-version and ADS authorization gaps remain open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Autoware documents an assumed Ackermann model distinct from the exact physical vehicle, with non-Ackermann output adaptation assigned to the vehicle interface; its converter expects same-type actuation status feedback and measures command-to-publish latency.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Branch-relative software docs; the adaptor is under development and feedback is steering-only. Software publication latency is not end-to-end bus or physical response latency, and no target vehicle was validated.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Specifies model, actuation-type and timing boundaries in a live implementation without claiming universal interface requirements or deployment assurance.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: PACMod3 maintainer documentation specifies accel/brake/steering command and report topics, DBC-version configuration, supported transports and a common-message boundary across DBC v3–12; some vehicle-specific CAN messages are unsupported.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: One hardware family; vehicle-specific manual, DBC and supported messages must be confirmed for the target vehicle. No interface timing, fault handling, installation or safety validation is established.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a primary implementation example of hardware/DBC configuration dependence; not generalized as a universal vehicle platform.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Autoware publishes mode, gear, longitudinal/lateral command-report, turn-indicator and hazard-light simulator compatibility procedures; generic coverage is manual and the automated suite is MORAI-specific.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Simulator checks do not establish hardware/bus compatibility, target-vehicle response, HIL/track correlation, fault coverage or safety validity; no tests were run in this review.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a bounded interface-test method and makes the simulation-to-vehicle validation gap explicit.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The official NATM guideline places scenario catalogues and simulation within a multi-pillar ADS validation framework that also includes track, real-world, audit/assessment and in-service monitoring evidence.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: The guideline is not a planning benchmark specification or proof that a planner is valid; only official indexed text for paragraphs 1-8 was inspected, and no local ODD or planning system was evaluated.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Distinguishes benchmark/tool evidence from broader system validation without changing the mapped planning claim or implying a universal test sequence.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The official NATM framework expressly separates virtual/simulation evidence from track and real-world testing, audit/assessment and in-service monitoring; it says a single methodology cannot comprehensively/effectively validate ADS safety.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Framework guidance does not establish controller performance, tire/vehicle model validity, target-vehicle results or the applicability of each pillar to a specific system; only indexed paragraphs 1-8 were inspected.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Strengthens the explicit boundary between simulation tools and deployment validation while leaving vehicle/ODD transfer evidence open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The adopted UNECE NATM guideline recommends scenario catalogues plus five complementary validation pillars—simulation/virtual, track, real-world, audit/assessment and in-service monitoring/reporting—and explicitly rejects reliance on one methodology alone for comprehensive ADS safety validation.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Guidance is not a binding approval or proof of a particular safety case. The direct PDF was inaccessible; content is limited to official indexed text at Section I paragraphs 1-8, and specific system applicability remains unassessed.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Directly informs the methodology comparison and makes the distinction between scenario coverage, simulation, physical evidence and audit traceable.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The official guideline frames virtual/simulation test tooling as one evidence pillar and pairs it with scenario catalogues, physical tests, audit/assessment and in-service evidence.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: The guideline does not qualify a specific simulator or prove sim-to-real fidelity; its publication and indexed scope do not replace the normative ISO/PAS 34506 text or system-specific validation.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Links the tool cell's explicit virtual-evidence boundary to the broader official ADS validation framework; simulator validity and physical correlation remain open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Lagos State Government identifies the Transport Sector Reform Law 2018 Part II sections 11-22 as the basis for state VIO duties/powers and distinguishes that state regime from the cited Abuja judgment.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Indexed government statement only; not enacted text, amendment history, complete road-rule model or ADS permission/prohibition. The Lagos full-law source remains inaccessible.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds jurisdiction-specific legal provenance without inferring that general VIO authority covers ADS deployment.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Official Lagos State material identifies its 2018 Transport Sector Reform Law as a state traffic/VIO authority source, distinct from general federal road-safety rules and international vehicle regulations.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Does not establish complete state law, federal/state conflict resolution, ADS authorization, vehicle type approval or Nigerian adoption of international standards; exact statute text and amendments remain unverified.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Makes the jurisdictional boundary explicit while retaining the legal authorization blocker.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The full-scale study models coupled lateral/longitudinal high-slip dynamics and combined tire slip; the snow/ice track experiment reports about 0.2-0.3 friction and a disturbance response, while documenting constant a-priori friction assumptions and force-model mismatch.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: One modified VW Golf GTI on a racing/handling track; friction uncertainty, diverse vehicles/ODDs, public-road transfer and repeatable physical comparisons remain unvalidated.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a full-text, physical low-grip case that specifies both vehicle-dynamics assumptions and where the estimator/transfer evidence stops.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: A research-stage nonlinear MPC alternative jointly optimizes online trajectory/control under coupled high-slip dynamics; it was compared against three other NMPC formulations in simulation and physically exercised on a full-size winter-track test vehicle.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: No repeatable physical lap-time comparison was made due to changing grip; the racing objective/ODD is not collision avoidance or public-road driving, and author-reported results were not independently reproduced.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a distinct high-slip NMPC design and a matched simulation comparison without treating its racing objective as the universal controller choice.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The full-text winter-track trial provides a concrete physical low-adhesion test with a logged snow-bank disturbance, but the same authors report varying grip, a constant a-priori friction assumption, documented model-force mismatch and no repeatable physical lap-time comparison.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: Single racing vehicle/track experiment; it does not validate urban traffic, the ODD, collision avoidance, simulator-to-road correlation, systematic fault coverage or a safety case.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a nuanced physical-validation case and explicit negative evidence about test repeatability and friction uncertainty; does not close the Safety gate.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Full-scale GTI experiments compare point-mass, single-track and two double-track model trajectories across ice/wet/dry surfaces. The point-mass trajectory produced a high-sideslip pendulum transient on linked icy corners; this is evidence that yaw/transient and per-wheel friction limits can matter in that ODD, not proof the most detailed model is always superior.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: One race/handling vehicle and extreme-maneuver tracks; author-reported results in a third-party-hosted accepted manuscript. Does not validate another target vehicle, public-road ODD, general model fidelity, fault response or safety.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Strengthens the physical foundation evidence while preserving surface-, vehicle- and objective-specific limits; state-estimation, actuator, ODD-transfer and fallback scope remain open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: This physical comparison adds model-fidelity choice as a consequential design dimension alongside geometric tracking and MPC alternatives: four optimized trajectory models were tested on ice, wet and dry surfaces, with a point-mass ice trajectory exhibiting a yaw/sideslip transient absent from the wet/dry observations. It supports conditional tradeoffs, not a universal algorithm or fidelity ranking.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: The tests concern extreme racing/handling maneuvers on one modified GTI; they do not compare production controller families under common public-road tasks or establish transfer, reliability or safety.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a full-text, physically tested alternative/design comparison and counter-search; broader deployed methods, target-vehicle transfer, faults and ODD coverage remain unresolved.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The study compares model-derived trajectories against a physical full-size vehicle on three surfaces and exposes a point-mass/yaw transient on ice. It is useful physical model-to-vehicle evidence precisely because the outcome is surface-specific; it cannot be treated as general simulator validation or safety proof.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: One vehicle, extreme-maneuver track ODD, author-reported test results and no independent reproduction located; no public-road hazards, comprehensive ODD/fault coverage or safety-case acceptance are tested.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a concrete physical evidence case and transfer boundary; the Safety/V&V gate remains open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The preprint distinguishes passive friction inference from deliberate high-slip excitation: a constrained longitudinal controller elicits tire-force observations, a simplified Magic Formula estimates friction locally, and repeated passes are aggregated spatially. It offers a concrete alternative to treating friction as known/constant, but friction estimates are offline and physically exercised only on one dry-concrete route.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: No independent ground-truth friction comparison, multiple surfaces/vehicles, online deployment, or public-road safety evidence is reported; this is an arXiv v1 preprint and the source's future-work section itself calls for broader conditions.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Strengthens the friction-estimation foundation and alternatives with full-text bounded evidence; state estimation, friction uncertainty, faults, and ODD transfer remain open.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: Adds an active friction-identification/control design: a constrained optimization objective trades estimation error and smoothness against acceleration and modeled car-following separation constraints, with repeated-location estimation reducing variance. The field maneuver is reported on dry concrete; safety constraints are simulation-tested rather than validated amid real traffic.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: One preprint, single vehicle/surface, offline estimation and no independent friction reference. It does not establish that deliberate high-slip maneuvers are suitable for all vehicles, traffic, road surfaces or ODDs, nor that this approach outperforms passive estimators generally.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a distinct active-excitation method to the current design alternatives without elevating it to a production recommendation or closing Control saturation.

cell_evidence_addenda.evidence_note: The paper's validation layers are separable: modeled worst-case car-following constraints are exercised in simulation, while the real-vehicle evidence consists of repeated high-slip estimation runs on one dry-concrete stretch. The latter supports physical feasibility in that test only, not real-traffic safety or simulator-to-road correlation.
cell_evidence_addenda.limitations: No real lead/follow traffic safety trial, multi-surface/multi-vehicle validation, independent friction ground truth, systematic fault or ODD testing, or safety-case argument is reported; arXiv v1, not peer reviewed in the inspected version.
cell_evidence_addenda.review_note: Adds a specific validation-evidence boundary and named residuals; Safety/V&V remains open.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: A peer-reviewed AVEC 2026 study proposes a risk-bounded predictive-control artifact in which MPPI generates a nominal shared-space vehicle command and a CVaR-CBF safety filter conditionally corrects that command under sampled pedestrian uncertainty. The repository abstract describes a carpark-style scenario and planned comparisons on collision rate, clearance, arrival and computation; full paper, numeric results, code and independent replication were not inspected.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: risk-filtered predictive-control command and simulated evaluation outputs
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Nominal MPPI command, vehicle state and acceleration/yaw-rate inputs, finite pedestrian-uncertainty samples, linearized barrier constraint and prescribed CVaR risk budget.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: A conditionally corrected first control command and simulated collision-rate, clearance, arrival-time and computation-time comparisons against MPPI and deterministic CBF baselines.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Repository abstract accurately summarizes the conference paper; conclusions are restricted to its carpark-style simulated scenario and stated model/sample assumptions.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: https://nottingham-repository.worktribe.com/output/66219629; indexed abstract, direct repository fetch returned HTTP 403.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: One recent research-stage control output example; it is not production practice or a standardized downstream interface.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Abstract/metadata only; no full methods/results, code, independent reproduction, real vehicle, public-road or general safety guarantee.

relationship_context.explanation: Corrected command is consumed downstream by a vehicle/actuation interface, but no universal message schema, timing/QoS contract or integration artifact is specified.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: The 2026 GRVA-26-27 ADS2 terms-of-reference proposal describes a future regulatory workstream to review and potentially amend UN GTR 26 and UN Regulation No. 185, maintain guidance/interpretation, cover DSSAD matters, and submit draft proposals by the January 2029 GRVA session. This is a proposed roadmap, not an adopted future standard or guaranteed amendment; the primary UNECE file was inaccessible for direct inspection.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: proposed ADS regulatory work programme and successor-standard roadmap
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Existing UN GTR No. 26, UN Regulation No. 185, guidance/interpretation and DSSAD matters considered by the proposed IWG on ADS2.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Potential draft amendments/proposals, maintained guidance and DSSAD-related work products targeted by January 2029 under the summarized terms of reference.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The secondary document record accurately summarizes the submitted proposal; direct primary text and formal disposition were not verified.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Official UNECE index https://unece.org/info/events/event/412104; registry summary https://globalautoregs.com/documents/43569; primary fetch returned 403.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Potential future international regulatory development as of 2026-10-27; no present requirement or national implementation inferred.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Secondary summary of a proposal; official primary text and meeting decision inaccessible. No adoption, final amendment or Nigerian applicability established.

relationship_context.explanation: Potential future standards/guidance may shape safety evidence if adopted; the proposal itself does not establish current compliance duties.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: UNECE's ADS 22nd-session document index lists an EC presentation titled Safety Performance Indicators (ADS-22-22r1), dated 7 Oct 2026, alongside an ADS2 IWG 2027 planning presentation (ADS-22-24). These are identifiable emerging regulator-facing evidence/planning artifacts, but underlying contents and future deliverables were not inspected; the record does not establish adopted indicators, required reporting schemas or future safety outcomes.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: regulator-facing safety-indicator and future work-plan presentation artifacts
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: ADS safety-performance-indicator concept and ADS2 regulatory work-planning inputs, as identified by titles and session listing only.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: A listed EC safety-performance-indicator presentation and Chairs' 2027 ADS2 planning presentation; actual schemas, metrics, milestones and decisions are not established from titles alone.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Official UNECE wiki search-index text accurately reflects document identifiers, titles, submitters and posted dates.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Accessible secondary record for ADS-22-22/Rev.1: https://globalautoregs.com/documents/43758, lines 152-180; official UNECE index identifies linked presentation, direct fetch returned 403.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Emerging regulator-session research artifact with prospective field-data follow-up; not an adopted standard or operationally validated output.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Secondary summary only; underlying presentation/methods unavailable, with no independent result, adopted metrics, mandatory schema or operational safety effect established.

relationship_context.explanation: The registry summary describes evidence candidates for in-service monitoring, but does not establish adoption or a required regulator/role deliverable.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: Linköping University and Lund University list a jointly organized Fall 2026–early 2027 PhD course in advanced motion planning and control, with tentative dates and eligibility limited to PhD students at ELLIIT partners. Its announced curriculum spans classical graph/lattice/sampling and differential-constraint methods, optimal-control/MPC, learning-based methods, uncertainty and multi-agent planning, plus implementation assignments; it is a restricted academic resource, not a general-access credential or evidence of completed delivery or learning outcomes.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: restricted PhD course and implementation-assignment learning resource
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: PhD participation at an ELLIIT partner; readings, selected planning/control algorithms, small implementation assignments, discussion and optional project.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Course participation and submitted implementation assignments; optional project presentation for additional 3 hp. The page does not specify public enrollment, fees or measured learning outcomes.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The institutional course page accurately describes the announced course; its tentative schedule and intended curriculum may change.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: https://isy.gitlab-pages.liu.se/fs/phd-courses/motionplanning/, lines 70-105; course content and eligibility lines 78-93, organization and examination lines 101-105.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: One restricted, announced near-future advanced learning resource; not a universally accessible credential or curriculum recommendation.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Tentative dates; eligibility limited to ELLIIT-partner PhD students; delivery, enrollment, cost and outcomes unverified. One course does not establish exhaustive learning-resource coverage or a universal progression.

relationship_context.explanation: The course spans planning/control methods and implementation tasks; it does not define a universal prerequisite order or learner route.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: A human-centered shared-control safety filter learns a neural state-action safety value from black-box interaction using model-free Hamilton-Jacobi reachability, then constrains a human-requested action with a Q-control-barrier function while minimizing deviation from that action. The RSS 2025 study evaluates the filter against last-resort filtering and no assistance in a racing simulator with 83 participants; this is one emerging control-design example, not road-vehicle or autonomous ADS validation.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: learned Q-CBF safety-filter design for human-shared control
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Simulator state, human nominal steering/braking request, learned state-action safety value function and explicitly defined action/failure sets for the racing ODD.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: A minimally modified control action that satisfies the Q-CBF safety constraint, plus intervention feedback to the driver.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The learned safety function is valid for the training/deployment dynamics and defined ODD. The paper's experiment uses Assetto Corsa, Silverstone GP, a BMW Z4 GT3, human steering/pedal inputs and a 30 Hz filter loop.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Oh et al., RSS 2025, arXiv:2504.11717v4, full paper: abstract pp. 1-2, lines 5-27; safety-filter/Q-CBF design Sections III-IV; simulator/ODD Section V, pp. 5-6, lines 530-564; 83-participant experiment Section VI, pp. 7-12; limitations Section VII, pp. 12-13, lines 1334-1364.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Emerging shared-autonomy control research applied to AI-assisted motorsports; race-track simulation is not public-road ADS operation.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: One simulator-based human study; no physical/public-road vehicle validation, road-transfer result, independent replication, broad production practice or regulatory evidence. The paper says the reactive filter addresses immediate threats but not strategic anticipation and raises possible over-reliance/cue effects. No safety guarantee beyond the learned ODD is asserted.

relationship_context.explanation: HCSF is compared with a last-resort safety filter for the same defined shared-control racing task. The intervention objectives differ; neither replaces nominal path tracking nor establishes an ADS-wide fallback design.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: World4Drive is a specific end-to-end planning algorithm that combines a multi-modal driving-intention encoder with a physical latent world model, predicts future latent states under candidate intentions, and uses a world-model selector to rank and select candidate ego trajectories. Its authors evaluate this algorithm on open-loop nuScenes and closed-loop NavSim; this is one benchmarked research design, not a general solution or road-validated planner.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: end-to-end intention-conditioned latent-world-model planning algorithm
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Multi-view RGB images; ego command and candidate trajectory vocabulary; spatial/semantic priors from pretrained metric-depth and vision-language models; temporal image context.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Multimodal candidate ego trajectories, predicted intention-conditioned future latent states, trajectory scores and a selected ego trajectory.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The implementation uses the paper's data/preprocessing, pretrained models, trajectory vocabulary and benchmark protocols. NavSim interpolates planner trajectories with an LQR controller; reported performance is conditional on the paper's comparator and evaluation setup.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Zheng et al., World4Drive, arXiv:2507.00603v1 (ICCV 2025), full PDF: abstract/Introduction pp. 1-2, lines 7-23 and 60-97; method pp. 2-4, lines 163-180 and 265-345; benchmarks/results pp. 4-6, lines 346-421; ablations pp. 6-7, lines 422-460.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Specific recent algorithmic frontier documented in an ICCV 2025 paper; the horizon reflects research maturity, not speculative status or established industry practice.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: One paper and selected open-/closed-loop benchmarks; no physical/public-road tests, independent replication, broad ODD/generalization, production prevalence, safety assurance or Nigerian transfer. Abstract and body give slightly inconsistent relative L2-error reduction values, so no such percentage is reported; code was described as forthcoming.

relationship_context.explanation: An algorithmic alternative to modular and other end-to-end planners only when sensor inputs, ego-trajectory output, timing and validation contracts match; the paper does not establish a universal preference or prerequisite.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: Interactive prediction-and-planning jointly models the effect of candidate ego behavior on surrounding-agent futures and selects an ego trajectory using those interactions; it contrasts with sequential pipelines that treat other-agent prediction as a one-way planner input. The 2026 review distinguishes marginal, conditional and interactive formulations and surveys time-axis, agent-axis and hybrid designs, while treating deployment and safety maturity as unresolved.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: interactive prediction-and-planning method family / joint modeling design
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Map and scene context, AV and surrounding-agent histories, candidate ego behavior/trajectory and conditional/interactive agent predictions.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Conditional or joint surrounding-agent trajectories and an ego trajectory; representation and interface vary across formulations.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The review defines marginal prediction, conditional multi-agent prediction and interactive ego-agent planning as distinct problem formulations. Suitability depends on the planner interface, scene representation, model coupling and evaluation conditions.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Li, Zhang & Zhao (2026), Artificial Intelligence Review 59:200, publisher full text, Sections 1-2, lines 71-116; Section 4.3; Section 5.2, lines 307-319; Section 6, lines 338-341 and 352-360.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Active research frontier documented by a 2026 review; classified in the future/futuristic horizon as a frontier item, not as speculative distant technology or universal production practice.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Review evidence supports taxonomy and research status only. No universal superiority, safety benefit, deployment prevalence or road-transfer guarantee is established; named primary methods require individual appraisal before detailed comparative claims.

relationship_context.explanation: Interactive joint modeling and sequential one-way prediction-to-planning are alternative architectures only when the target ego-motion decision, output, timing and validation contracts are comparable; neither is a mandatory universal learning prerequisite.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: TARGET is an emerging research toolchain that converts traffic-rule text into a validated functional-scenario DSL, instantiates simulator-specific scripts, and records ADS behavior for violation analysis. Its authors report testing seven ADSs with 284 scenarios derived from 54 rules across CARLA, LGSVL and MetaDrive, surfacing 610 issues; two were confirmed by developers. This is research evidence, not proof of tool adoption or ADS safety.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: LLM-assisted traffic-rule-to-simulation scenario generation and monitoring toolchain
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Traffic-rule text; functional-scenario elements; simulator/map dictionaries and templates; ADS under test; generated scenario execution traces.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Validated abstract scenario descriptions, simulator-executable concrete scripts, recordings/logs and issue reports for rule violations, collisions or timeouts.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The paper's supported rule vocabulary, maps, traffic-rule interpretation, templates, simulator adapters and tested ADS versions apply. LLM self-validation and syntax alignment reduce but do not eliminate incorrect rule interpretation; findings depend on oracle, scenario and simulator validity.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Deng et al., IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering 51(7), 2025, pp. 1950-1968; arXiv:2305.06018v4 full HTML: framework/DSL §§III-A-B, rule parsing/validation §III-C, script synthesis §III-D, monitor §III-E, experiments §§IV-V, validity threats §VII, future direction §VIII; official open-source repository README and scenario DSL example.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Emerging research toolchain for rule-derived simulation tests and ADS issue discovery; publication and open-source code do not establish commercial use, standards conformity or safety acceptance.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: One research framework; simulated evaluations across seven selected ADSs and 54 rules, not a representative fleet or exhaustive traffic-rule set. Only two findings were developer-confirmed; issue counts are not incidence rates, real-world safety effects or approval evidence. Traffic-rule scope, map coverage, simulator fidelity, geographic/legal variation, model versioning, reproducibility and current maintenance require independent review.

relationship_context.explanation: Rule-derived scenario generation complements formal scenario specifications, scenario libraries, runtime monitors and physical validation; it does not replace those independent assurance layers.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: ScenicProver is a research-stage compositional assurance method for learning-enabled cyber-physical systems: it combines assume-guarantee contracts, simulation-based probabilistic evidence, user-supplied formal proofs and imported assumptions, then composes evidence into system-level guarantees and a provenance-tracked assurance case. Its AEB case study uses assumed sensor guarantees and simplified physics; the authors explicitly leave sim-to-real validity to future work.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: compositional probabilistic assume-guarantee safety-assurance method
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Component interfaces and contracts, Scenic scenario distributions/simulator traces, independently generated proof results, imported external assumptions and confidence levels.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Sound lower bounds on contract-satisfaction probabilities under stated independence and modeling assumptions; composed system-level contracts and an assurance case with evidence provenance.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Component contracts and interface model are valid; evidence-generation independence conditions hold; simulator distribution represents the modeled environment; imported manufacturer guarantees and supplied proofs are correct and applicable. The AEB case study also uses simplified physics.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Vin et al., ScenicProver, arXiv:2511.02164v1 (2025), full HTML: abstract and framework scope lines 45-85; evidence assumptions and sim-to-real statement §4.1 lines 184-211; combined contract evidence/assurance case §5; AEB case study §6; generated assurance-case examples Appendix 0.C.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Research frontier for composing heterogeneous formal, probabilistic and assumed evidence over learning-enabled ADS components; the horizon reflects a preprint/tool-framework example, not accepted certification practice.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Preprint research framework and simplified simulation example, not a vehicle deployment, certification method acceptance or real-world safety result. Conclusions rely on formalized components/contracts, evidence independence, scenario distributions, imported manufacturer assumptions and simplified physics; no physical test or independent replication is reported in the inspected case study.

relationship_context.explanation: Compositional contract evidence can organize test, proof and external-assumption results alongside safety cases and scenario validation; it does not replace safety engineering, independent evidence review or physical/operational validation.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: ScenicProver is a research-stage software framework built on Scenic that supports component/interface modeling, assume-guarantee contracts, simulator-based probabilistic verification, Lean 4 proof integration, evidence composition and automatic assurance-case generation. The paper demonstrates the tool on simulated AEB; it does not establish code availability beyond its statement that case-study code is in a repository, tool qualification, deployment or safety approval.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: probabilistic/formal verification and assurance-case software framework
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Scenic system/scenario descriptions, component interfaces, contracts, simulator traces, proof files, imported assumptions and verification confidence settings.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Component/system probabilistic evidence, composed assurance-case tree with provenance, Lean 4 proof obligations and textual evidence visualizations.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Compatible Scenic simulator and modeled component APIs; soundness assumptions of proof/test procedures; correct contract formalization, external evidence and independence conditions. The paper says full case-study code is in a repository but no independently verified repository URL or build was reviewed here.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Vin et al., arXiv:2511.02164v1, full HTML §§1, 3-6 and Appendix 0.C; framework capabilities and Lean 4 integration lines 61-85; implementation details lines 226-230; authors state full AEB code is in a repository at lines 310-314.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: A research software framework for integrated evidence management over learning-enabled ADS components; future/futuristic describes its research-stage scope, not verified future adoption.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Preprint research implementation; no independent installation/build, tool qualification or external user/adoption evidence inspected. AEB case is simulated and simplified; no physical vehicle or road validation. Formal and probabilistic outputs depend on modeled environment and supplied contracts/assumptions; tool output is not itself a safety certificate.

relationship_context.explanation: The framework can organize proof and testing artifacts for an assurance case, complementing scenario-generation, safety-case review and physical V&V tools; it does not replace their evidence or acceptance.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: Two foundational international standards distinguish different automotive safety problem classes: ISO 26262:2018 addresses hazards from malfunctioning safety-related E/E systems across the vehicle lifecycle, while ISO 21448:2022 (SOTIF) addresses unreasonable risk from functional insufficiencies and reasonably foreseeable misuse in intended functions that depend on situational awareness. Their scopes are complementary, not interchangeable; both are published editions marked by ISO as to be revised, and neither alone is ADS approval or proof of safety.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: complementary functional-safety and SOTIF standards
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Safety-related E/E system/function, lifecycle and malfunction hazards for ISO 26262; intended functionality, situational-awareness dependence, functional insufficiencies and reasonably foreseeable misuse for ISO 21448.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Frameworks and lifecycle activities for managing functional safety and SOTIF design, verification, validation and operation; exact normative work products require the licensed standard texts.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Application is within each standard's stated production-road-vehicle and E/E/intended-function scope; the relevant edition and national/contractual applicability are confirmed for the target vehicle and jurisdiction.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: ISO 26262 official series record https://www.iso.org/publication/PUB200262.html and ISO 26262-1:2018, -2:2018, -4:2018 catalogue abstracts; ISO 21448:2022 official catalogue https://www.iso.org/standard/77490.html, abstract/exclusions and lifecycle stage 90.92 ('to be revised'). Public catalogue records only; normative text not inspected.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Established foundational international safety standards for road-vehicle E/E systems and intended-function safety; standards are distinct by hazard scope and are not a complete ADS safety case or regulatory approval framework.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Only official public catalogue abstracts/status were inspected, not full normative clauses; no conformity or certification conclusion can be made. ISO 26262 addresses malfunctioning E/E behavior and does not address nominal performance; ISO 21448 excludes ISO 26262 faults and cybersecurity and is not intended for functions with established trusted V&V measures. Both cited editions are marked 'to be revised'; draft/replacement content and national adoption were not reviewed. Neither is a standalone ADS approval or full safety-case standard.

relationship_context.explanation: ISO 26262 and ISO 21448 address different but potentially interacting hazard classes; ADS-level safety-case, cybersecurity, scenario/ODD validation and regulatory requirements remain separate evidence and applicability questions.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: SAE J3292:2026 specifies an infrastructure-led Automated Vehicle Marshalling architecture for low-speed, geofenced private controlled environments; its public scope summary allocates destination assignment/route planning, localization, path determination, trajectory calculation and vehicle motion control across the infrastructure/vehicle system. It is a specialized V2X AVM standard, not a general public-road ADS planner specification; ASIL-related functional-safety requirements are explicitly outside its stated scope.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: V2X infrastructure-led automated-vehicle-marshalling technical standard
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Vehicle/mission destination, infrastructure sensing and guidance, vehicle/infrastructure wireless messages (IMM/VMM), perceived objects/obstructions and controlled-environment operating state.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Destination assignment and route planning, localization, path determination, trajectory calculation, OEDR and vehicle-motion-control allocations across the AVM system; interoperability-oriented messages and functional lifecycle states.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The SAE page's summary accurately reflects the paid standard's scope; operation is at controlled speeds in a geofenced private controlled environment with infrastructure-assisted sensing. The normative full standard was not accessed.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: SAE Mobilus official J3292_202604 record, published 2026-04-13; public scope/functional allocation summary: geofenced private controlled environment, low-speed L4 AVM architecture and listed destination assignment, route planning, OEDR, localization, path determination, trajectory calculation and vehicle-motion-control functions; explicit ASIL-related requirements exclusion. SAE topic page lines 220-226.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Emerging standardization example for specialized automated vehicle marshalling; a scoped infrastructure-led Level 4 private-environment use case rather than general route/motion planning for public-road ADS.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Public publisher summary only; full normative requirements, message schemas and conformance tests were not inspected. Scope is AV marshalling/private controlled areas, not open-road general ADS planning; no deployment prevalence or operational safety evidence is established. SAE summary explicitly puts ASIL-related functional-safety requirements outside scope; applicability, interfaces and legal approval remain separate.

relationship_context.explanation: The standard's function allocation gives a specific planning-to-localization/trajectory/control interface example under infrastructure-led AVM; it is not a universal planner architecture or curricular prerequisite.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: Two employer-hosted motion-planning vacancies describe planner engineers changing behavior/path/lane/speed-planning features and evaluating performance through simulation and vehicle tests. Woven by Toyota names interfaces with perception, control, simulation, infrastructure and tooling, plus CI/HIL/in-vehicle testing; Zoox names interfaces with perception, prediction and operations and simulation, closed-course and on-road review. These are employer-specific examples, not a universal planner API or hiring standard.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: Employer-specific planning-engineering output and verification workflow
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Maps, sensor/perception and prediction context, ego/road state, planning features and scenario/test data, as described in each posting.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Planner behavior/path/lane/speed feature changes and performance improvements; test evidence from simulation and, depending on employer, CI/HIL, closed-course, in-vehicle or on-road review. Exact trajectory/API schema is not specified.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The postings accurately describe each employer's vacancy at access date; duties and interfaces may change by role, team and geography.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Woven by Toyota posting, responsibilities/qualifications lines 19-34; Zoox posting, role overview lines 12-19 and qualifications lines 23-31; both full employer-hosted pages inspected 2026-10-26.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Current employer-specific role evidence for planner outputs and downstream verification/team interfaces; not universal occupational or architecture guidance.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Two current employer postings only; not a representative labor-market sample, formal planner-controller message contract, safety case or product-performance evidence. Job language and vacancies may change.

relationship_context.explanation: The postings connect planning feature work to downstream testing/review but name different team interfaces; treat these as employer-specific handoffs, not a universal org chart.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: Authoritative university teaching resources provide complementary foundations for automated-vehicle planning: CMU's 18-744 course distinguishes route planning and path planning within the AV stack, while MIT's archived 6.882 course covers deterministic/probabilistic/learned planning and robot motion planning, including A*, configuration-space and sampling-based search. These are examples of instructional scope, not a universal curriculum or credential.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: University course and archived learning-resource examples
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Learner preparation and goals; the CMU course description spans AV sensing through control, while MIT's course page lists computing/probability prerequisites and planning-theory topics.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Instructional coverage of route/path planning in an AV architecture and of discrete, continuous, sampling-based, probabilistic and learned planning topics; no learner outcome is claimed without outcome evaluation.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Official pages accurately represent their respective course scope and dates; archived material may remain useful but availability and current course details may differ.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: CMU 18-744 official course page lines 10-27 (last modified 2024-11-22; Spring 2025 latest listed offering); MIT 6.882 archived page lines 3-12 and 30-32.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Established planning-learning-resource examples spanning a vehicle-specific architecture course and a historical cross-domain planning-theory course; neither establishes a required sequence or 2026 availability.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Two institutional pages, not a systematic curriculum inventory, credential standard, efficacy study or universally recommended sequence. MIT 6.882 is historical; CMU's latest listed semester is Spring 2025. Neither substitutes for jurisdictional road rules, ODD or safety instruction.

relationship_context.explanation: The vehicle-specific CMU course provides stack context while MIT's historical course supplies general planning theory; their scopes complement rather than prescribe prerequisite ordering.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: A future-facing planning research capability is to evaluate candidate ego trajectories against action-conditioned future scene evolution and feed those predicted outcomes back into planning, rather than relying only on current observations or post-hoc scoring. ProDrive's 2026 CVPR workshop prototype demonstrates one query-centric planner/BEV-world-model coupling on NAVSIM v1; this is a research direction, not evidence of future industry adoption or validated road competence.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: candidate-conditioned future-scene reasoning for trajectory planning
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Multi-view camera images, LiDAR, ego state, candidate trajectories and planner-refined ego tokens; predicted BEV scene rollouts and learned reward signals condition candidate evaluation.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Multiple candidate ego trajectories, predicted future BEV scene states, candidate reward scores and a selected trajectory; future-aware gradients train the planner/world-model coupling.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The model's predicted future BEV features and reward labels remain sufficiently informative for the represented NAVSIM distribution; the benchmark does not establish robustness outside that distribution.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Fu et al., ProDrive, full arXiv manuscript Sections 1-3, PDF pp. 1-5 (planner/world-model architecture and coupling); Sections 4-5, pp. 6-8 (NAVSIM v1 test, metrics, ablations and future work).
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: A future-facing research capability documented by a present-day workshop prototype; horizon describes potential direction, not a prediction of deployment or curricular priority.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: One workshop study on a log-derived, non-reactive NAVSIM benchmark with 136 test scenarios; no public-road/closed-loop vehicle validation, independent replication, broad ODD coverage, calibrated uncertainty or adoption evidence. The authors list more expressive world models as future work.

relationship_context.explanation: ProDrive couples prediction and planning internally, contrasting with reactive or modular pipelines and external post-hoc trajectory reranking; it is one research alternative, not a proven replacement.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: ProDrive exposes a research-prototype planning output bundle: multiple ego trajectories, candidate-conditioned future BEV scene predictions and learned reward scores used to select one trajectory. This is an internal benchmarked model output, not a published planner-controller interface or production downstream contract.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: candidate trajectory and predicted-future/reward output bundle in a research prototype
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Multi-view images, LiDAR, ego status, refined ego queries and K candidate trajectory proposals.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Candidate ego-centric trajectories (paper implementation K=64, eight waypoints over a four-second horizon), future BEV states per candidate, learned reward scores including collision/drivable-area/TTC/progress/comfort factors, and selected candidate trajectory.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Paper-specific NAVSIM setup and its learned reward/simulator labels define the meaning of the score; those outputs are not standardized across planners.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Fu et al., ProDrive, full arXiv manuscript Figure 2 and Sections 3.1-3.4, PDF pp. 3-5; Sections 4.1-4.3, pp. 6-7.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: A future-facing research output structure from a present-day workshop prototype, evaluated on logged-data NAVSIM; future adoption and external interface conventions are unknown.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: One research prototype and log-derived benchmark evaluation; no real-time vehicle interface, controller-consumed trajectory schema, actuator command, on-road test or safety certification is shown. K and horizon values are implementation settings, not general requirements.

relationship_context.explanation: The selected candidate is the planner's research-system output; the paper does not establish its downstream controller message contract or organizational owner.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: A peer-reviewed autonomous-racing study describes a combined policy/controller output chain: risk-conscious jump-start reinforcement learning trains a trajectory-planning/motion-control policy, while nonlinear MPC generates locally optimal commands constrained by vehicle dynamics to follow a designated trajectory. The abstract does not define actuator-level messages or establish road-vehicle transfer.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: Risk-conscious RL policy and nonlinear-MPC motion-command output chain
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Learned racing policy trained using expert initialization/curriculum and risk-conscious mutation; designated trajectory and modeled vehicle state/dynamics are inputs to NMPC.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Policy-selected trajectory/motion behavior and locally optimal nonlinear-MPC control commands that satisfy modeled vehicle-dynamics constraints; exact steering/throttle/brake message format is unspecified in the abstract.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Track-map scenarios, expert/guide policy, training setup and nonlinear vehicle model adequately represent the racing task; these assumptions are not shown to hold for public roads or other vehicle platforms.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Hou et al., PubMed PMID 40030835, abstract lines 228-232; bibliographic record lines 177-190, DOI 10.1109/TCYB.2024.3518697. Full IEEE text remained inaccessible.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Emerging research example from autonomous racing; it describes a learned policy plus model-based command-generation interface, not normal road-car control practice.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Abstract-only evidence; full article, quantitative results, test protocol, actuator schema and independent replication were not inspected. No road transfer, safety certification or real-world deployment is established.

relationship_context.explanation: The abstract places NMPC command generation downstream of a designated trajectory within the combined racing framework; it does not establish a general RL-to-MPC architecture or production actuator contract.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: An established ADS test-design technique organizes scenarios in a multidimensional matrix of ADS feature, ODD elements, OEDR behaviors and failure-mode behaviors, then develops preliminary procedures, data collection, metrics and success criteria across modeling/simulation, closed-track and open-road test components. NHTSA's 2018 framework is explicitly preliminary and reports that its project conducted no physical testing.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: scenario test-matrix design and multi-modal ADS testing technique
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Selected ADS feature and intended ODD, OEDR capabilities/behaviors, tactical maneuvers, expected objects/events, failure modes and mitigation strategies, facilities/personnel, data collection plan and performance/success metrics.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: A multidimensional scenario/test matrix, sampled preliminary procedures and performance measures, linked to distinct simulation, closed-track and open-road test components.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The report selected three conceptual ADS features and developed sample procedures from generic ODD/OEDR and failure-mode analyses; the framework is illustrative and developers must adapt boundaries, scenarios and criteria to the actual system.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: NHTSA report DOT HS 812 623 (2018), Executive Summary PDF pp. iii-v (ODD, OEDR, scenario-matrix dimensions and test architecture); report PDF pp. 19-20 (no physical testing), pp. 98-109 (FMEA and fail-operational/fail-safe analysis). The front-matter suggested citation has a title mismatch, so claims use the report title/number and inspected technical sections only.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Established/traditional ADS test-design technique documented in a 2018 U.S. government-sponsored preliminary framework; it is not a binding requirement, complete standard or evidence of current field practice.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: 2018 report, historical U.S. framework and only three selected sample features; the report says its feature list is not exhaustive and no physical tests were conducted. Its front-matter suggested citation conflicts with the report title, so bibliographic attribution needs independent verification. It does not establish scenario completeness, simulator fidelity, road safety or regulatory acceptance.

relationship_context.explanation: Modeling/simulation, closed-track testing and open-road testing are treated as distinct test-architecture components with different advantages and limitations; the report does not establish that any single component or fixed sequence is sufficient.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: An emerging operational-safety hazard-analysis method combines Event Sequence Diagrams, Concurrent Task Analysis, STPA and Fault Tree Analysis across system, scenario and hazard-identification stages to model interactions among L4 driverless ADS fleet vehicles, remote operators and operational personnel. Its published demonstration is a bounded MaaS fleet case, not a validated universal safety method or proof of risk reduction.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: integrated operational hazard-identification and scenario-modeling methodology
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Fleet/ADS system boundary, agents and their functions/tasks, operational phases and scenarios, initiating events, control interactions, human-task dependencies, failure modes and available operational evidence.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Structured hazard scenarios/catalog, event sequences, interaction/task models, unsafe control actions, fault-tree contributors, responsibilities and candidate safety requirements or mitigations; models can inform but do not themselves complete quantitative risk assessment.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The paper's ESD, CoTA, STPA and FTA descriptions and its single L4 MaaS case support a contextual method claim. Different system scope, operational phases, expertise and data can change the methods' relative contribution and outputs.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Correa-Jullian et al., full open-access SAGE article: abstract lines 29-32; method comparison Table 1 lines 107-120; operational case analysis and results at lines 315 onward and 620-647, including method-specific overlap and limited operational data.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Emerging research method published online in 2024 for operational safety of driverless L4 ADS-as-a-service fleets; maturity reflects a proposed integrated approach, not established universal practice.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: One on-route passenger phase of a modeled driverless L4 MaaS fleet; the study reports that only 13% of failure modes were identified by all three compared methods, with method-specific unique contributions, and warns results depend on analysis. Limited operational data constrained risk quantification. No field effectiveness, complete safety case, comparative universal superiority or reduction in actual incidents is established.

relationship_context.explanation: ESD/FTA represent event sequences and causal combinations, while CoTA/STPA address task and control interactions; the paper combines them because their modeled aspects differ, not because every ADS requires this exact stack or order.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: An emerging vehicle-integration foundation is understanding how a service-oriented Adaptive Platform can coexist with Classic ECU software through standardized interfaces and signal-to-service translation, and how redundant service instances may support fail-operational designs; CAPI 1.0 adds a common implementation initiative, but platform capability is not proof of any vehicle's redundancy or safety behavior.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: distributed automotive software-platform integration and fail-operational architecture concepts
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Adaptive applications/services, Classic-platform signals and control values, software/runtime services distributed across ECUs, and a fault condition affecting a primary service instance.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Standardized service communication and translation across Classic/Adaptive boundaries; platform-level option to mirror a service and switch to a secondary hardware instance after primary failure.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: AUTOSAR documents platform capability and architectural intent. Actual redundancy depends on implementation, hardware, configuration, timing, fault coverage and vehicle-level safety design; CAPI release does not itself validate those properties.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: AUTOSAR Adaptive Platform page, lines 148-163: service-oriented runtime, standardized interfaces, Signal-to-Service Translation, redundant service mirroring/takeover and Classic/Adaptive coexistence; CAPI 1.0 release page, lines 141-150, identifies the 2026 executable implementation and code generators.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Emerging integration foundation as of 2026-10-26: platform capabilities have existed in the Adaptive standard, while the common executable implementation is newly released. Neither maturity label means universal industry use.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Official standard/issuer pages only; no full technical specification, CAPI code, fault-injection test, timing analysis, safety case, implementation conformance or vehicle deployment was inspected. Licensing/access and independent adoption remain unresolved.

relationship_context.explanation: Classic and Adaptive can coexist and translate signals/services at their boundary; redundant service execution can complement fault-tolerance design but does not replace end-to-end vehicle safety analysis or evidence.
