matrix_claim_mappings.claim: CoCoSaFe is a research-stage offline code-level verification method combining ODD/behavior formalization, compositional contracts, controlled-invariant safe sets and bounded model checking for traditional ACC/LKA controller code, with a BMC/neural-verifier decomposition for DNN controllers. It is one formal-assurance frontier candidate, not an accepted certification method or full-ADS safety case.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: compositional formal code-verification method for ADAS controllers
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Controller code; analytical longitudinal/lateral behavior and safety specifications; modeled environment and ODD; assume-guarantee subsystem contracts; computed invariant safe sets; bounded model-checking limits; neural-network verifier for DNN components.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Conditional offline proof or falsification verdict for specified controller implementations over modeled invariant safe sets/ODD; the paper reports seven ACC/LKA controller implementations evaluated in minutes on a workstation. It does not output a regulator certificate or prove whole-vehicle safety.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Claim depends on correctness and adequacy of analytical models/specifications/ODD, subsystem-contract validity, invariant-set computation, verifier soundness and sufficient BMC loop bounds. Evaluation is limited to selected ACC and lane-keeping models/controllers.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Nenchev et al., Journal of Systems and Software 230 (2025), 112499, published PDF: https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/document/3553193; method Sections 4.1-4.3.2 (pp. 3-8), evaluation Section 5 (pp. 8-10), validity/future work Section 6 (pp. 11-12), DOI 10.1016/j.jss.2025.112499.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Future/futuristic frontier candidate because this recent peer-reviewed method remains research-stage and the authors identify broader ODD/controller evaluation as future work; horizon is a maturity classification, not a prediction of adoption.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: One study with no physical vehicle/public-road validation, full ADS assurance, tool qualification, regulator acceptance, certification or independent replication. Authors note the need for complementary data-driven testing and future urban/adverse-weather/other-controller studies; formal results remain conditional on specification/model/tool assumptions.

relationship_context.explanation: Formal controller-code verification can complement scenario/data-driven testing and broader safety-case evidence by checking code against a modeled safe set; neither method subsumes the other, and this paper does not establish a complete ADS safety case.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: Compositional controller assurance requires explicit analytical behavior/safety specifications and an ODD, subsystem assume-guarantee contracts, and control-invariant safe sets; the CoCoSaFe study treats these as prerequisites for conditional code-level verification, not universal proof obligations or accepted certification criteria.

matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: System/controller boundary and ODD; analytical behavior and safety requirements; modeled environment and subsystem assumptions; assume-guarantee interfaces; candidate safe set and dynamics used to establish control invariance.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Structured assumptions, guarantees and modeled safe conditions for conditional subsystem reasoning; not an executed verification result, safety certificate or proof of complete ADS safety.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The selected ODD/boundary is adequate; requirements represent intended behavior; environment and subsystem contracts and invariant sets are sound and mutually consistent. One ACC/LKA research framework is the evidence base.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: A research foundation for safe learning-based control is to model the admissible state-dependent action set explicitly and parameterize policy updates so actions are sampled within it; convergence and hard-safety claims depend on known safe-action constraints, deterministic dynamics and stated policy/step-size assumptions. AISTATS 2024 validates the approach on simulated inverted-pendulum and quadcopter tasks, not a road vehicle.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: safe reinforcement-learning foundations for constrained policy-gradient control
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: State/action spaces, deterministic transition model, known safe set and state-dependent safe actions, differentiable stochastic policy, reward, safety constraints and an admissible step-size schedule.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: A policy-gradient update that samples within a specified safe-action set, with convergence to stationary points under the stated theorem assumptions; not an automotive controller or road-safety certificate.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: Safe action sets are known and have positive bounded measure; deterministic dynamics, reachability, policy regularity and theorem step-size conditions hold; the safe-set characterization is valid.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Suttle et al., AISTATS 2024, PMLR 238, pp. 4420-4428: Section 2, pp. 2-3; Section 3, pp. 4-6; Section 4, pp. 6-8; conclusion p. 8. Full PDF https://proceedings.mlr.press/v238/suttle24a/suttle24a.pdf.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Future-control foundation candidate from general nonlinear-control research; simulated quadcopter/pendulum results are adjacent theoretical evidence, not vehicle-control demonstrations.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: No automotive model or experiment, vehicle-specific safe-set estimation, physical validation, ODD transfer, safety case, independent replication or certification. The authors explicitly leave safe-set learning and real-world robotics application for future work.

relationship_context.explanation: Provides general safe-RL foundations complementary to vehicle-specific control work; it does not establish method transfer to road vehicles or replace vehicle-specific validation.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: ConvIO is a 2026 research method for designing centralized zonal automotive E/E architectures: its five-step process assigns I/O to chassis-aware zones, selects zone counts/locations, and generates communication paths around an HPC. In a single BEV-model case study, the authors report 68.7-69.9% lower combined LV cable length than a domain-oriented baseline across three network topologies; this is not evidence of production deployment, safety validation or universal optimality.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: metrics-driven zonal I/O allocation, zone-placement and network-routing method
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Vehicle chassis graph and I/O locations, functional grouping and candidate zone counts; chassis-aware shortest-path distances; vehicle model and comparison baseline; bus, redundant-bus or star-ring communication topology and selected linkage/optimization parameters.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: Suggested number and placement of zonal aggregators, I/O-to-zone assignments and communication routes to a central HPC; comparative combined LV cable-length metric. No validated runtime API or safety case is output.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: I/O coordinates, chassis graph and vehicle model represent the evaluated platform; chosen cost metric and communication topology are suitable for the design question; reported comparison uses the same modeled I/O population and baseline assumptions.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Mauser et al., IEEE Access 14 (2026), pp. 98616-98632, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3707952. Full published text: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/408232334_ConvIO_A_Framework_for_Convergence_of_Inputs_and_Outputs_in_Automotive_Zonal_EE_Architectures; institutional record: https://portal.fis.tum.de/en/publications/convio-a-framework-for-convergence-of-inputs-and-outputs-in-autom/.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Future/futuristic candidate for next-generation SDV/zonal E/E integration methods, published in 2026; the horizon is not evidence of production maturity or adoption.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: Single modeled BEV case and reported wiring-length outcome; generalization across platforms/I/O distributions is unproven. Full production constraints, independent reproduction, timing/cybersecurity and comprehensive functional-safety analysis are not established; fault-containment extensions are future work.

relationship_context.explanation: A physical E/E architecture-design method complementary to software/middleware/interface design; it does not define service APIs or prove a complete or universally optimal vehicle architecture.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: ConvIO's future-zonal design uses a distinct algorithmic stack: k-d-tree mapping of I/O to chassis connection points, k-means/elbow heuristic for initial zone count, Dijkstra-derived chassis path distances for hierarchical agglomerative refinement, and greedy nearest-neighbor communication-path generation. The paper tests this stack in one modeled BEV case; it does not prove globally optimal zoning or deployed network performance.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: chassis-aware clustering and communication-route generation algorithm stack for zonal I/O integration
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Chassis graph, I/O and attachment locations, candidate number of zones, chosen clustering linkage, aggregator candidates, HPC location and selected bus/redundant/star-ring communication topology.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: I/O clusters/zones refined by chassis path distance and a generated communication tree/path set to the HPC; the paper compares total modeled cable length, not optimality guarantees or live-network QoS.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The chassis graph and I/O coordinates capture relevant geometry; heuristic-selected cluster count and linkage are suitable; the greedy routing output is an acceptable candidate for the modeled topology; objective prioritizes the reported cable-length comparison.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Mauser et al., IEEE Access 14 (2026), pp. 98616-98632, DOI 10.1109/ACCESS.2026.3707952; full published text Sections V.A-V.E and Algorithms 1-6 (PDF pp. 4-8), with validation and limitations in Sections VI-VIII. Author-uploaded full text: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/408232334_ConvIO_A_Framework_for_Convergence_of_Inputs_and_Outputs_in_Automotive_Zonal_EE_Architectures; TUM institutional record cross-check.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Future/futuristic algorithm candidate for designing zonal SDV E/E integration; research implementation and one modeled case do not establish deployment or adoption.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: The paper combines heuristics and a greedy route method; global optimality is not established. One BEV-model scenario, limited cable-length KPI and no independent implementation/reproduction; latency, network load, fault containment, cybersecurity, production routing constraints and cross-platform robustness are not validated.

matrix_claim_mappings.claim: Näke et al. formulate zonal control-unit placement and component assignment as a p-median/location-covering integer linear program, and cable routing as a capacitated multi-commodity-flow integer linear program minimizing wire length. The exact optimum is conditional on the stated graph, objective and constraints; evaluation uses a simplified vehicle topology and synthetic randomized nets.
matrix_claim_mappings.item_type: optimization method: zonal placement/assignment and capacitated cable-routing ILPs
matrix_claim_mappings.inputs: Simplified vehicle topology, candidate ZCU locations, component/I-O assignments, point-to-point communication nets, capacities and wire-cross-section assumptions.
matrix_claim_mappings.outputs: ZCU placement and component assignment, communication routes and modeled wire-length/objective values.
matrix_claim_mappings.assumptions: The stated graph and linearized objective/constraints represent the design problem; randomized netlists and wire areas represent the modeled workload. Optimality is only for this mathematical model.
matrix_claim_mappings.locator: Näke et al., Efficient Architecture Evaluation and Generation of Automotive Wiring Harnesses, IEEE ITEC Asia-Pacific 2025, DOI 10.1109/ITECAsia-Pacific63742.2025.11345003; full five-page author-deposited paper, Sections II-V: https://www.ifte.de/mitarbeiter/lienig/ITEC_AP_2025.pdf; TU Dresden institutional publication record: https://fis.tu-dresden.de/portal/en/publications/efficient-architecture-evaluation-and-generation-of-automotive-wiring-harnesses(724c6c22-aba8-4b64-a244-932c01ab6a71).html.
matrix_claim_mappings.area_context: Emerging optimization formulation for zonal E/E architecture and harness design in a 2025 peer-reviewed conference paper; it is a design-stage research method, not evidence of deployed OEM practice.
matrix_claim_mappings.claim_limit: One five-page study with synthetic workloads on one simplified base-vehicle topology. It omits ZCU-to-ZCU wiring and detailed 3D/circle-packing feasibility; no independent reproduction, production harness, timing/QoS, EMC, power integrity, installation, safety validation or full cost/weight objective was inspected. No head-to-head comparison with ConvIO was conducted.

relationship_context.explanation: Conditional alternative to ConvIO's clustering and greedy routing for zonal placement/assignment and route design only when topology, constraints, objective and required outputs are made comparable; neither study establishes universal superiority.

cross_area_candidates.explanation: Autoware planning interface defines a trajectory for the controller to follow; this is a specific documented handoff. Path/trajectory generation remains distinct from feedback tracking.
Autoware control emits normalized control commands consumed/adapted by the vehicle interface; the adapter may convert to vehicle-specific actuation and returns measured status.
Scenario/ODD-based evaluation tests planner performance; simulation evidence complements but cannot replace physical testing or system-level assurance.
Control constraints and failure/fallback behavior can be assessed in component/system V&V; no evidence makes one specific controller an assurance requirement.
Interfaces, status, timing, diagnostics and mode transitions contribute evidence/assumptions to V&V; architecture adjacency alone is not an approved learning or safety dependency.

Other-agent prediction and scene interpretation can inform planning; the selected canonical area is Perception and Scene Understanding. Prediction remains a possible function/interface within that area, not a separately created area or a claim that all planners consume the same prediction output.

counter_searches.result: Material nuance found: nuPlan-R reports changed planner comparisons with reactive multi-agent agents; Paden's full survey documents established graph/search, sampling/tree and variational-optimization families. The MIT plan describes proposal-stage RRT and layered planning with known dynamic-traffic limits. The Stanford Junior report documents historical integrated planning and a planner-to-controller handoff. The BeTop paper gives one emerging joint prediction/planning method; NAVSIM is a non-reactive logged-data tool, while CARLA 2.1 is a distinct reactive simulator with version-specific metric changes. The full CommonRoad competition report compares reachability plus optimization against trajectory sampling/evaluation under shared scenarios, model, feasibility checks and compute budget, with only two systems entered. The official FRSC 2025 training compendium directly supplies locally grounded cues and hazard conditions for scenario/ODD context, but it is not a complete current legal rule inventory or ADS authorization instrument; the FRSC regulation PDF returned 404 and Lagos law pages timed out. The added official FRSC cross-check finds the 2024/2025 compendia list NRTR 2004/2012/2016 as reviewed, one implementation document distinguishes the 2016 amendment, the RTSSS page cites NRTR 2004 as scheme origin, and the 2025 post refers to NRTR (2024) without an authenticated Gazette. This improves provenance but does not establish the current consolidated law. Local rule semantics, uncertainty/fallback, licensing, more planner families and physical validation remain unresolved, so the area remains open.

established model-based control software chronology and vehicle-dynamics simulator capabilities
dual-motor steering fault detection and passive/active fault-tolerant alternatives with reported simulation/HiL evidence
ALKS failure transition demand, severe-failure MRM, traffic-aware stop behavior and current R157 revision status
LPV static-output-feedback torque-vectoring alternative under steering loss-of-effectiveness and saturation
closed-loop fault-injection toolchain, degraded-state signaling, anti-windup/speed-reduction counteractions and metric disagreement
low-grip sideslip/friction state-estimation performance and missed transitions under insufficient vehicle excitation
extreme-adhesion constrained-MPC alternative with abstract-only field-test evidence
HIL-to-track correlation using physical brake hardware/production ECUs and simulator/model discrepancy
counter_searches.result: The full 2024 controller comparison and official Autoware documentation establish model-dependent foundations. O'Kelly's results are one modeled I-80 case; GUARD uses ten five-parameter scenarios and one metric; Zhao et al. identify unresolved stopping-rule, residual-risk, and fidelity assumptions. Nigerian ADS authorization, full ODD/fault coverage, human factors, empirically validated simulator/physical safety evidence and role breadth remain open; this is not area closure.
